### [RT @IFM_AI: Looking for a reference manual for building a frontier LLM? We wrote one 👇 The K2 Horizon technical report …](https://x.com/_akhaliq/status/2122839570274455764)

`x:@_akhaliq` · T1 · 2026-11-17 23:49 UTC · en · by AK

> RT @IFM_AI: Looking for a reference manual for building a frontier LLM? We wrote one 👇 The K2 Horizon technical report is now on arXiv: 13…

> 來源提供的正文:
> RT @IFM_AI: Looking for a reference manual for building a frontier LLM? We wrote one 👇
>
> The K2 Horizon technical report is now on arXiv: 134 pages on how we built six models, from architecture to inference. It may be the most detailed LLM training reference you can read today.
>
> • Architecture: we bring two new attention designs, MoVA and softplus attention gating, to strengthen reasoning. With them, our 36B model nearly matches a 32B dense one on one-seventh of the active parameters.
> • Pre-training: we trained four models, from 3.7B to 36B, on the same 22T tokens. Their normalized loss curves collapse onto nearly the same line, so a recipe that works on a small model carries over when scaling up.
> • Data: 60+ pages on the part most reports skip. How we generated ~10T synthetic tokens, and why we chose the data mix on predicted scores at scale, which reversed the small-run ranking.
> • Post-training: we document our full production-scale run for the 375B flagship.
> • Inference: Uno gives an autoregressive model diffusion speed with one small adapter. Up to 2.2× faster decoding, lossless by construction, no draft model.
>

> 來源提供的正文:
> Instead of moving computation to a separate container to provide isolation, Codex uses OS-level sandboxing to constrain commands running in the user’s existing environment.
>
> For example, consider using Codex to develop an iOS app on a Mac. If you decided to sandbox Codex by running it inside Docker, Codex would not be able to run the iOS build toolchain composed of native Mac executables, nor could it launch the iPhone simulator to run the code.
>
> A Docker-based workflow could delegate builds and simulator operations to the Mac host, but those operations would execute outside the container’s sandbox and would need their own restrictions.

> The default permission profile disables network access. When a command requests access, Codex may prompt the user directly or route the request to auto-review. If your build regularly downloads from

> 來源提供的正文:
> The default permission profile disables network access. When a command requests access, Codex may prompt the user directly or route the request to auto-review.
>
> If your build regularly downloads from a package registry, you can allow the registry’s domain in a permission profile with the network proxy enabled. The proxy checks each request against the profile’s domain rules to decide whether to forward it. Matching requests don’t need separate network approval each time.
>
> The network proxy’s core request-handling and policy logic is shared across all three major operating systems. Proxy setup and sandbox integration are OS-specific.
>
> On Linux, the command connects to a listener inside its isolated namespace. A process outside the sandbox relays those connections to the configured proxy.

`x:@tetumemo` · T1 · 2026-11-17 23:30 UTC · en · by テツメモ｜AI図解×検証｜Newsletter · ♥ 5 · 💬 1

> 📝こんな作り方があったのか、、、私もNTPの動画で試してみよう！Seedance 2.5で、開始画をそのまま渡すと動きが悪くなる。その代わりに「背景だけ」を渡すと、描写性能をフルに引き出せる https://t.co/03jGPNAp5i かし子さんの発見だ 今までの作り方 ・各カットの開始画をSeedance 2.5に渡す https://t.co/hcxKTR4hyf

> 來源提供的正文:
> 📝こんな作り方があったのか、、、私もNTPの動画で試してみよう！Seedance 2.5で、開始画をそのまま渡すと動きが悪くなる。その代わりに「背景だけ」を渡すと、描写性能をフルに引き出せる
> https://t.co/Wo61KqITyA
>
> かし子さんの発見だ
>
> 今までの作り方
> ・各カットの開始画をSeedance 2.5に渡す
> ・意図したカットにはなるが、それはそれは動きの悪い動画になる
>
> 今日試した作り方
> ・開始画の代わりに、背景だけを渡す（開始画から人物を消す、という考え方でもいい）
> ・参照として渡すのは、キャラクターシート＋小物等のシート＋各カットの背景のシート
> ・プロンプトで各場面の背景を@で紐づける
>
> これなら意図したカットを作りつつ、Seedance 2.5の描写性能をフルに引き出せている、と本人の感触だ
>
> 参照に完成画を渡すと動きが死ぬ感覚は、私の動画作りでも覚えがある
> 生成と編集はCapCut AI（動画スタジオのSeedance 2.5 Flash）でやったそうだ

> 來源提供的正文:
> 📝アニメ好きだからこれは興奮する！『チ。』の構想段階のプロットが、公式に公開された
>
> 『チ。』プロット資料、設計の中身を棚卸しする
> 魚豊十周年展の公式が公開した、構想段階のプロットから読めること
>
> 【主人公の設計】
> ・1代目：10歳の天才少年。人を見下す「嫌な奴」として設計され、1話だけ登場
> ・2代目：18歳前後。最初から天才ではなく、途中から研究に目覚める、感情移入しやすい側
> ・3代目：遊牧民。盗みに入った家の書物を読み、集団で唯一字が読める。先代の研究を見て地動説に取り憑かれる
>
> 【データのリレー】
> ・1代目は、火星の逆行運動などの「歯抜けデータ」を隠して死ぬ
> ・2代目は、年周視差の公式や楕円のアイデアを残す
> ・3代目が、ほぼ完成まで持っていく
>
> 【ヴィランの設計】
> ・派遣異端審問官。普通のくたびれたおっさん、中間管理職風、公務員風
> ・地動説にも信仰にも本当は興味がない。家族を養うためだけに仕事をしている
> ・「悪役だが、"悪"のように単純には絶対書かない」と明記されている
>
> そして最終話
> 主人公達の積み上げたデータの断片を見つける青年の名が、アルベルト・ブルゼフスキであると明かして終わる、と最初から書かれていた

### [California tells Waymo to take the next exit after freeway mishaps](https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/11/18/california-tells-waymo-to-take-the-next-exit-after-freeway-mishaps/5310841)

`rss:theregister_security` · T2 · 2026-11-18 17:45 UTC · en

> Robotaxi operator suspends driverless rides on high-speed roads nationwide after construction zone incursions and a run-in with patrol vehicles

> 來源提供的正文:
> Waymo has suspended driverless freeway rides across the US after California regulators intervened over robotaxis entering construction zones and trying to bypass highway patrol vehicles. California's DMV banned Waymo from offering driverless trips on its freeways on Wednesday, November 11. The same day, Waymo pulled the handbrake on its freeway services countrywide. The move affects all areas in which Waymo operates on freeways, including San Francisco, Los Angeles, Miami, Phoenix, and Austin. The Alphabet-owned company has not indicated how long the suspension will last. Waymo says freeway testing will continue with trained specialists behind the wheel. Jonathan Groveman, spokesperson for the California DMV, told the Associated Press that the organization imposed the ban following two incidents involving Waymo's robotaxis that posed an "imminent hazard to public safety." On November 5, three of the company's driverless cars entered an active construction zone on US 101 near Burlingame, south of San Francisco. The second incident occurred the following day, and in footage shared widely online, a Waymo vehicle can be seen trying to drive around highway patrol vehicles conducting a traffic break – a maneuver used to slow or stop traffic. "The Department determined that Waymo's driverless freeway operations pose an imminent hazard to public safety due to recurring incursions by its vehicles into active construction zones where construction workers, vehicles and equipment are present," Groveman said in the statement. Groveman said the DMV had already imposed restrictions and required corrective action following similar incidents on May 18. Waymo subsequently recalled nearly 4,000 cars after some were caught ignoring road closure signs and cones designating construction zones in Phoenix and San Francisco. A separate recall covered software affecting nearly 3,800 robotaxis over problems including slowing on high-speed roadways and driving into floodwater. A Waymo spokesperson said that despite California's temporary ban, its robotaxis continue to operate on city streets across the US. "Safety is at the foundation of everything we do," they said. "Following recent freeway construction zone encounters on US 101 in California that did not involve any injuries or collisions, the California DMV has implemented an operating restriction on freeway operations in the state. "In alignment with our safety-first principles, we have also temporarily restricted freeway operations across our other operating markets to evaluate our performance. Our ride-hailing service continues to operate safely on surface streets, serving over half a million trips each week. "We are working with the California DMV and other state officials diligently and responsibly to resume freeway operations." Other nuisances and hazards caused by errant Waymos include clogging traffic in thick fog, driving into telephone poles, and killing cats and dogs. ®

`rss:theregister_security` · T2 · 2026-11-18 17:23 UTC · en

> In today's how-could-things-get-worse-for-Microsoft news, it seems someone's GitHub org admin creds have been compromised

> 來源提供的正文:
> Microsoft’s official agent framework package hosted on PyPI has been hijacked and now installs info-stealing malware, multiple security research firms have discovered. CEO Satya Nadella may be on stage trying to wow investors and customers at his company’s annual Ignite conference, but somewhere in the bowels of a building in Redmond his open source team is likely panicking at what appears to be unauthorized access to an administrator account on Microsoft’s Github organization. The problem package is Microsoft’s agent-framework, versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2, researchers reported late yesterday and this morning. According to OX Security, version 1.26.1 was reverted to a safe version, but the attacker later uploaded 1.26.2 through Microsoft’s official PyPI publisher account, suggesting that, at least at the time of their report, the credentials hadn’t been locked down. Safe to say, but if you find either version in your environment assume you have some account security work to do. Microsoft agent-framework for Python boasts nearly 200,000 downloads a month and is used to build and deploy AI agents. As of those latest releases, it’s also being used to exfiltrate environment variables, credential files, and other secrets for Azure, Git, Docker, Hugging Face, and other sensitive developer services. To make matters worse, the package never needs to be imported to do its dirty work – all it takes is a Python interpreter with the package installed to start up – the infected package still pulls the genuine 1.26.0 version of Microsoft’s agent-framework in order to keep itself running and looking legitimate, while in the background it gathers up credentials, encrypts them as a base64-encoded chunk of JSON, and sends them off to a webhook.site address hard coded into the malware. It appears from researcher accounts that this is made to act fast, as the malware isn’t persistent and only runs as long as the malicious version of the agent-framework remains in a site-packages directory. What it does do, however, is not just look for credentials in the environment: It actually starts calling for new ones and collecting them, too. In particular, the malware requests fresh identity tokens from GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, and Azure itself, which are exfiltrated to the same webhook site. “That combination of passive theft and active token requests makes it especially dangerous in cloud build environments, because even short-lived tokens are useful when they're exfiltrated right away,” said researchers at OpenSourceMalware. The agent-framework GitHub repo is offline as of writing. It’s been pointed out online that Microsoft’s repo for ONNX Runtime, an AI accelerator, is also offline. Other Microsoft repos remain available, and neither Microsoft nor security researchers have linked the ONNX repo’s pull to the malware campaign. “We have made some repositories private while we investigate malicious content,” a Microsoft spokesperson told The Register. “Our priority is to protect customers and the broader ecosystem. We are working to review and will take further action as needed.”® Updated at 1805 with comment from Microsoft.

### [Cyber insurers now want proof you can actually recover](https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/11/18/partner-content-cyber-insurers-now-want-proof-you-can-actually-recover/5309325)

`rss:theregister_security` · T2 · 2026-11-18 16:00 UTC · en

> PARTNER CONTENT: As carriers tighten underwriting, a backup job marked green is no longer enough. Here’s the evidence underwriters expect

> 來源提供的正文:
> Cyber insurance pricing has cooled. Marsh’s Global Insurance Market Index shows global cyber rates falling for a 13th consecutive quarter, with US rates recently stabilizing after the ransomware-driven spikes of 2020 and 2021. Part of the reason rates are lowering is because carriers are imposing stricter requirements that determine if you will qualify at all. A major global carrier recently stopped writing law firms altogether because of claims volume, and brokers expect healthcare and managed service providers (MSPs) to be next. The newest requirement is the one many MSPs are least ready for: proof that you can actually recover. This is what insurers really want to see, and meeting the bar is harder than it sounds. Why insurers stopped taking backups on faith In a recent webinar with cyber insurance provider Beltex, the familiar list of requirements came up first:  Multifactor authentication (MFA) on external access and privileged accounts  Endpoint detection and response (EDR) on every endpoint  A staffed 24/7 team where managed detection and response (MDR) is required, and timely patching.  Backup is now joining that list, and for good reason. For years it was assumed that having backups and a green job status was good enough. Claims have shown otherwise. Now, attackers go after backup infrastructure to make their ransomware more effective, and an untested restore can re-infect the production network. Beltex described an MSP that restored a client directly from backup without involving the insurer. The attackers were still in the environment, and the ransom reportedly doubled. So, carriers are asking for proof. Some want evidence of a successful restore within the last six months, and some insurance applications must be signed by a C-level executive rather than the IT director to put ownership behind it. Proof of speed matters as much as proof of recovery Being able to recover is only half the question, because time is where claim costs balloon. Insurers, it turns out, don’t object to paying claims. They object to paying big ones. Beltex’s favorite example involved an 85-person firm hit through a zero-day firewall flaw. Their MDR solution contained the intrusion in about 20 minutes, forensics confirmed two servers were touched, and clean backups had the firm fully functional within 36 hours. The claim came in at around $85,000. Compare that with downtime and business interruption: a firm billing $10,000 a day that is offline for a week loses $70,000 in income before recovery costs and claim submission. Yet large servers can take four to 24 hours to restore. That is why underwriters care how fast you can come back and how successfully. Where you recover is the other half Speed raises a second problem: where do you restore to? Breach counsel treats the first 72 hours as the most critical window, and incident response (IR) teams need to isolate and investigate infected systems during it. Restoring into production too early risks reintroducing the threat and disturbing the evidence investigators need. Waiting for a safe place has the clock running. Recovery that is fast but not safe doesn’t satisfy anyone. Meeting all of this is harder than it looks Put the pieces together and the bar is high:  Backups you have actually tested  Recovery times you can state and meet  And a clean, separate place to recover to  Underwriters want to know whether you exercised reasonable care, so a row of green checkmarks won’t do. Run a test restore. Confirm you’re protecting everything that matters, including the server someone labeled “not in production.” Have the business owner, not just IT, confirm the right systems came back within agreed recovery time objectives (RTO) and recovery point objectives (RPO), and keep the logs, screenshots and sign-off in your ticketing system. It doesn’t need to resemble a government audit; Beltex noted that this alone puts you ahead of most organizations. Where cloud disaster recovery fits Cloud-native disaster recovery changes the equation. Cove’s DRaaS solution lets teams stage a pre-recovered VM in the N-able cloud that can be failed over to in about 15 minutes, off the production network. That answers the speed question and the location question together. Forensic investigators can validate and hunt in the sandbox while the business keeps moving, with rollback to earlier points in time. Once everyone agrees the recovery point is clean, workloads can run from the cloud over VPN, and failback uses recovery agents to bring changes home. Where to start Insurance is a financial failsafe, not a substitute for a bad data protection posture. Start by listing what the business couldn’t lose for 72 hours, set recovery targets, test them and document the results. Check the policy itself: a standalone cyber policy rather than a small add-on to a general one, with a limit of at least $1 million, and $2 million as the business scales. And if an incident does hit, disconnect affected machines from the network rather than powering them off, so forensic data survives. N-able Cove Data Protection, recognized as a Champion in the Infotech 2026 Enterprise Backup Data Quadrant, provides cloud-native data protection for organizations. Learn more at n-able.com/products/cove-data-protection. Contributed by N-able.

### [AI-powered cyber threats are changing the rules of enterprise recovery](https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/11/18/sponsored-ai-powered-cyber-threats-are-changing-the-rules-of-enterprise-recovery/5310515)

`rss:theregister_security` · T2 · 2026-11-18 15:00 UTC · en

> SPONSORED POST: As cyberattacks become more sophisticated, organizations need to look beyond prevention and ensure they can recover critical data quickly and reliably

> 來源提供的正文:
> Cybersecurity has long been a contest between attackers finding new ways in and defenders trying to keep them out. Artificial intelligence is making that contest more complicated, giving cybercriminals new ways to develop and adapt their attacks while putting additional pressure on conventional cyber defences. For enterprise IT leaders, the challenge extends beyond preventing a breach. What happens when an attacker gets through? Can compromised data be identified, clean copies recovered, and essential systems brought back online without prolonged disruption? These questions are becoming increasingly important as organizations confront both traditional threats and emerging AI-powered cyberattacks. A successful defense strategy must, therefore, account for what happens after an incident, not just the measures designed to prevent one. Making recovery part of the defence This is where cyber-resilient enterprise storage has an important role to play. Rather than relying solely on traditional backup processes, organizations need ways to protect critical data, detect potential compromise, establish which copies can safely be recovered, and restore those copies as quickly as possible. Infinidat addresses this challenge through its InfiniBox and InfiniBox SSA enterprise storage platforms, which incorporate the company’s InfiniSafe cyber resilience and recovery software suite. InfiniSafe combines immutable snapshots, which cannot be altered or deleted during their protected retention period, with logical air-gapping to isolate the management plane from the data plane. Fenced forensic environments provide a separate space for validating data before recovery. The technology also supports automated cyber protection, allowing security monitoring data center wide cyber security software applications or a Security Operations Center (SOC) to automatically talk to InfiniBoxes and trigger immutable snapshots when suspicious activity is detected. This helps reduce the window in which critical data might be exposed. For organizations concerned about recovering compromised information, optional InfiniSafe Cyber Detection uses AI-based analysis to help identify cyber affected data and locate the last known good copy of the data for recovery. Speed is another consideration. Infinidat guarantees recovery of immutable snapshots in one minute or less for InfiniBox and InfiniBox SSA, subject to the guarantee’s terms and conditions. Ultimately, cyber resilience isn’t about assuming every cyberattack can be stopped. It’s about ensuring that when defences are breached, organizations have the tools and processes to recover trusted data and limit the operational consequences. For enterprise IT teams, that makes recovery readiness an essential part of the cybersecurity conversation. Sponsored by Infinidat

### [UK MPs want AI watchdog with power to pull the plug on dangerous models](https://www.theregister.com/ai-and-ml/2026/11/18/uk-mps-want-ai-watchdog-with-power-to-pull-the-plug-on-dangerous-models/5310567)

`rss:theregister_security` · T2 · 2026-11-18 09:30 UTC · en

> Parliamentary committee says tech giants can't be left to mark their own homework when it comes to AI safety

> 來源提供的正文:
> UK MPs want a watchdog with the power to pull the plug on dangerous AI models, rather than leave the likes of OpenAI and Anthropic to decide when they've gone too far. In a report shared with The Register ahead of publication on Wednesday, a parliamentary committee is calling for an AI Safety and Security Bill that would give a watchdog powers to intervene while models are still being developed. It could halt high-risk training and testing, block deployments, or suspend AI services if the risks can't be contained. LLMs are trained on billions of learned parameters and so developers can't always predict what a model will do in every situation. The recommendations come from Parliament's Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee, which questioned researchers, former AI employees, and representatives from OpenAI, Google DeepMind, Anthropic, and Meta. All four companies assured MPs they wouldn't release models they considered unsafe. The trouble is, they don't use the same yardstick for safety, and UK law doesn't generally require them to get an independent opinion before releasing anything. "We cannot give today’s AI leaders unfettered freedom to behave like modern-day Dr Frankensteins, creating dangers beyond anyone’s control," said committee chair Liam Byrne MP. Just as with aviation, pharma or nuclear safety, UK government want to rely on manufacturers' assurance alone, and want regulation. "Our hearings exposed gaps in independent scrutiny, incident reporting and powers to stop unsafe systems. Once some models are released, they cannot reliably be recalled," added Byrne. "Protection must begin while systems are being built and tested." The committee's report, Guardrails for Growth: Making AI Safe, identifies ten holes in Britain's approach to AI safety, including the lack of mandatory incident reporting, limited access for independent testers, and inadequate protections for whistleblowers. The UK already has an AI Security Institute (AISI), which has made a name for itself testing some of the world's most powerful models, but its work depends on voluntary cooperation, and it has no authority to stop a company releasing a model that raises safety concerns. MPs want AISI to continue its testing work while a separate regulator takes responsibility for enforcement. Developers of designated high-risk systems would have to provide evidence supporting their safety claims and give independent researchers access to examine them. Significant changes to a model's capabilities or safeguards would trigger further scrutiny. Former AI employees also told MPs that raising safety concerns can come at a price. Restrictive contracts, commercial pressures, and financial disincentives can all discourage staff from speaking out, the committee heard. MPs want stronger legal protections for whistleblowers and compulsory reporting of AI incidents and near misses. There's a fair bit of money riding on this, too. Using OECD productivity estimates, the committee calculates that AI could leave Britain's economy up to £400 billion larger over the next decade. It also sees an opportunity for the UK to make money from independently testing AI models, building on the expertise already established at AISI. MPs argue that stronger safeguards could encourage businesses, particularly smaller firms, to adopt the technology. "AI firms must be required to substantiate their safety claims, independent experts must be able to scrutinize them, and a regulator must have the power to intervene when risks cannot be controlled," Byrne said. "Ministers, accountable to Parliament, must decide what risks the public should be asked to bear." MPs want the new laws on the books in the next parliamentary session, and say Britain should use its turn at the G20 helm in 2027 to get other countries on board with tougher rules for AI testing, incident reporting, and risky model releases. Whether ministers are prepared to hand a watchdog the power to stop AI development is another matter. The committee's recommendations aren't binding, and the government has yet to commit to the proposed legislation. ®

### [Oracle reveals fix-this-ASAP-grade Java4Shell bug that allows attacks on many third-party apps](https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/11/18/oracle-reveals-fix-this-asap-grade-java4shell-bug-that-allows-attacks-on-many-third-party-apps/5310661)

`rss:theregister_security` · T2 · 2026-11-18 04:33 UTC · en

> Attackers can crash the JVM or achieve unauthenticated RCE

> 來源提供的正文:
> The United States Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has urged Java users to immediately patch a high-severity flaw in the software, which attackers can use to crash the Java virtual machine or achieve unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE). Oracle revealed the flaw in its monthly patch dump for November, which offers 655 patches, 62 of them rated critical, affecting 62 products. Several of the flaws are rated more dangerous than the Java problem, CVE-2026-114938, which Big Red didn’t single out as worthy of special attention despite CISA’s warning. The cyber-agency’s decision seems apt because vulnerability research and red teaming outfit Calif.io, which discovered the flaw, used its X account to claim news of the problem had leaked before public disclosure and the release of Oracle's fixes. By then, Calif had already tested the flaw, which it named “Java4Shell,” and found applications including Keycloak, Atlassian’s Jira and Confluence, Jenkins, Apache Kafka Broker, and Elasticsearch are susceptible to RCE. Calif, which also helped to find the PHP2Shell flaw, says the flaw is a memory-corruption vulnerability in OpenJDK's Base64 decoder. “Base64 is a very common way of representing binary data as text. It is used in authentication protocols, to encode file uploads, and to deliver network messages,” the company explained. “To decode Base64 faster, OpenJDK uses specialized x86-64 CPU instructions to process many bytes at once.” “We discovered a bug in that optimized machine-level code that lets malformed input overwrite neighboring memory. With careful exploitation, the corruption can reveal sensitive memory, as Heartbleed did, or lead to remote code execution. The corruption itself can be triggered by just 64 A characters followed by a single =:” Calif applied the CVSS 4.0 bug-rating scheme and gave the flaw a critical-rated score of 9.2/10. Infosec outfit SentinelOne’s analysis suggests the flaw “sits in the Java standard library, so exploit traffic is specific to each application.” “Any Base64 value an application passes to java.util.Base64.Decoder can carry the payload, including HTTP Basic credentials, SAML artifacts, CSRF tokens, and MIME encoded words. In default configurations of the affected applications listed above, attackers can reach this code path prior to authentication.” Cisco’s Talos security team pointed out that the flaw is present in OpenJDK Java versions 17.0.6 and later running on x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 VBMI (Vector Byte Manipulation Instructions) support enabled. “These vulnerabilities have already been tested against a suite of Java applications with success, but the attack surface is likely much larger as additional targets are tested and confirmed,” Talos advised. Cisco’s infosec experts urged adoption of the fixed versions of Java Oracle posted on Tuesday but noted it is possible to mitigate the flaw on x86-64 machines by starting the JVM with support for AVX-512 disabled. Akamai’s Chief Information Security Architect Jan Schaumann, writing on the Openwall project’s mailing list, expressed a little discomfort with Calif’s work. “Calif.io set their priorities on publicity-maxxing, it seems,” he wrote, pointing out that the flaw-finding firm’s announcement of Java4Shell opens by stating “After we disclosed PHP2Shell, we realized many people didn't know what PHP was. So we decided to go after something a little more familiar: Java.” Talos’s analysis of Java4Shell includes the interesting observation that it “has not observed in-the-wild exploitation of this vulnerability yet. However, we anticipate probing attempts may pick up soon after public disclosure.” That second sentence perhaps supports Calif’s assertion that news of the flaw leaked before disclosure. The rest of Big Red’s flaws Java4Shell deserves a place high up on patch priority lists. So do the six 10.10 flaws Oracle reported, three in its Access Manager product, one in the Oracle Platform Security for Java, another in the WebLogic Server, and one in Business Intelligence Enterprise Edition. Big Red also repaired five 9.9-rated bugs, in Oracle Text, Hyperion, RDBMS, and Autovue. The November patch dump also includes 28 flaws rated 9.8/10. By Tenable Security’s count, 249 of the patches are for high severity bugs. Oracle’s Hyperion enterprise performance management accounts for 267 of the bugs. Such is life in the age of AI-powered flaw finders – which Calif says burned through just $200 worth of tokens to find Java4Shell. ®

> BBC

> ,

> ,
> Ledger
> and

> , was exacerbated by the reality that few popular websites enforce strict rules on the sources of third-party content.
> The Zoom.com homepage loading the malicious JavaScript file from Optimizely. Image: blog.report-uri.com. Click to enlarge.
> According to a blog post from the security firm
> Report URI
> , on November 16 malicious JavaScript code was served to visitors of 178 organizations through Optimizely’s platform. Report URI researcher
> Scott Helme

> Helme noted the affected websites also served exploit code custom made to attack known vulnerabilities in older Apple iPhone and iPad devices. Known by such names as “
> DarkSword
> ” and “
> Coruna
> ,” these are zero-click exploit kits that chain together a half-dozen security holes to seize complete control over outdated devices and extract data.
> “The important lesson here is that trusted JavaScript doesn’t always remain trustworthy,” Helme
> wrote
> . “A website can be compromised through a third-party dependency without its own code or infrastructure ever being breached.”
> Contacted for comment, Optimizely said that on November 16, 2026 it “identified a security incident in which an unauthorized party exploited a vulnerability in the Optimizely Experimentation to add malicious JavaScript to some customer projects.”
> “We acted swiftly to contain the incident and have fully remediated the identified vulnerability,” reads a written statement shared by Optimizely. “These measures included blocking access to the vulnerable path, deploying a fix, removing the injected code from affected projects, ending active sessions, revoking tokens, and resetting access for affected user accounts. We have also implemented additional protections to prevent malicious code from being delivered in Cloudflare. While the incident has been fully remediated, we are working with third-party experts on a comprehensive investigation.”
> Many top web properties no longer fully display content unless visitors agree to let often dozens of third parties serve JavaScript, a powerful web scripting language that enables interactive content. JavaScript code is run on the user’s device, and it can read information displayed in the user’s browser and even modify a website’s appearance or content.
> One reason JavaScript is so heavily used is that it enables fairly precise browser fingerprinting and other ways of tracking visitors and clicks. According to the
> 2025 Web Almanac
> by HTTP Archive, the median homepage loads at least 22 JavaScript files. But as the incident with Optimizely shows, a compromise at a third-party vendor’s website can quickly snowball into a supply chain attack against downstream websites that end up serving visitors tampered and malicious JavaScript files.
> Zach Edwards
> is a researcher at
> Infoblox
> and the co-founder of the ad-tracking service
> DecryptAds
> . Edwards said Optimizely is a vendor which often collects data outside of consent flows, with their JavaScript snippets being embedded as close to the top of the page as possible to ensure that it’s one of the first things to render, which is important since the product is primarily built for A/B testing.
> “So to make the product work as expected, this code is setup to fire immediately on-page load, and not restrict rendering behind a consent dialog box,” he said. “This means that this supply chain attack didn’t require any clicking or consent to trigger — most of the impacted clients would immediately serve up the payload as soon as someone loaded the page, further increasing risks from this type of JavaScript snippet being compromised.”
> Websites can minimize the chances that a breach at a third-party content provider spirals into a supply chain attack by taking full advantage of “
> Content Security Policies
> ” or CSPs, which specify the domain names that are allowed to serve third-party content. But Edwards said most websites — apart from perhaps the largest e-commerce, social media and financial platforms — don’t even bother with CSPs, or else tend to leave them overly permissive for marketing reasons.
> “With literally all websites which embed 3rd party JavaScript resources, if you don’t have a content security policy then if any of those partners get compromised, new domains can be injected into your website via JavaScript which won’t be stopped,” he said. “We’re in the age of JavaScript supply chain attacks and yet almost no one is talking about why content security policies were invented and how this is largely the solution for operators, even though it’s not always simple to get it initially deployed.”
> How broadly deployed were CSPs at the websites impacted by the Optimizely attack? According to Report URI, 68 of the sites had no CSP at all, while 50 of them had a CSP that still allowed the malware payload
> and
> the data theft. The company found only 24 of the affected sites (15 percent) had CSPs that fully blocked the malicious payload.
> Image: blog.report-uri.com.
> The overall deployment of CSPs across the Web’s busiest sites is somewhat lower — about 10 percent — according to Helme’s site
> crawler.ninja
> , which scans the top million websites daily for security issues. Helme said he hopes this incident will encourage more sites to adopt effective CSPs, noting that it could have been far worse: By Report URI’s estimates, the purveyors of this malware attack managed to steal only around $7,500 worth of virtual currency from affected users, as well as an unknown number of payment card records.
> Helme said he often compares the current widespread lack of CSPs to the Wild West.
> “Organizations are running all this code, but they don’t know what it’s doing,” Helme said in an interview with KrebsOnSecurity. “This is why we keep seeing such large scale breaches in places [where] there are no checks and rules in place on the code we’re running, so this was kind of inevitable. Once an attacker gets to the point of running code on your site, the question is what do they want to do with that and can they write the script to do it. Now with AI that’s not a problem anymore.”
> Internet users can control the JavaScript elements allowed to run on webpages by using simple script-blocking plugins like NoScript. But these tools have always only been effective for diehard security and privacy nerds who are willing to put up with sifting through dozens of JavaScript requests on each new website.
> Happily, modern ad blocking software can handily block most third-party JavaScript requests. Ten years ago, the standard security advice for end users was to install antivirus and enable a firewall. These days, your ad/script blocker
> is
> your firewall. We explored several options and approaches to blocking ads in our August 2026 story,
> Who’s Tracking You?
> Update, Nov. 18, 7:06 a.m.:
> Optimizely has published
> a report
> (PDF) on its initial findings about the attack.

### [Daily disruptive outages that ground planes and halt work – welcome to the new normal](https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/11/17/daily-disruptive-outages-that-ground-planes-and-halt-work-welcome-to-the-new-normal/5310634)

`rss:theregister_security` · T2 · 2026-11-17 23:41 UTC · en

> NSA, Apple add to a week of high-profile network outages, largely attributed to 'routine maintenance'

> 來源提供的正文:
> Another day, another disruptive network outage (or two) as government officials and company execs scramble to assure an anxious populace that these are not coordinated cyberattacks – and security experts call this the new normal. A classified network that the US National Security Agency uses for internal communications, called NSANet, went offline on Tuesday in what the agency described as a “temporary degradation during scheduled routine maintenance.” “While some internal systems were affected, mission-critical capabilities remain fully operational and our ability to defend national security continues,” the NSA said in a statement following media reports about the outage. “NSA's infrastructure is designed with multiple layers of redundancy to maintain operations during planned maintenance or unexpected events.” Around the same time, Apple users began reporting issues across multiple services – including Apple Support, iCloud, the App Store, Apple Pay, and more – with Apple retail stores worldwide also reportedly experiencing disruptions that halted sales and in-person support. A day earlier, customers at major US banks including JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, and US Bank reported service outages that Chase attributed to “a software bug in on-premise hardware systems - there is no evidence this is cyber-related.” All of these high-profile outages followed last week’s US Federal Aviation Authority (FAA) order grounding all planes on Friday due to problems with copper wiring during an L3Harris network upgrade, and a Microsoft 365 outage on Thursday. Redmond later blamed the massive service disruption on a faulty software update it pushed back in July. Despite the weekend respite from network outages, your humble vulture still had to field is-this-the-beginning-of-the-end questions from friends and family all day Saturday and Sunday, most of whom suspected Russia or China – maybe even Iran – caused the spate of downed systems and services. A highly sophisticated, coordinated nation-state hack would be a much more exciting cause for the disruptions. The real culprit, however, appears to be aging, under-funded infrastructure, riddled with decades-old bugs and held together by digital sticks and glue. “As someone who started out as a hacker, I know how tempting it is to connect the dots when major systems fail one after another,” Remedio CEO Tal Kollender told The Register, adding that there’s “no credible public evidence that these outages were part of a coordinated cyberattack,” and most have been attributed to technical failures. “What concerns me more is what these incidents reveal about the fragility of our digital infrastructure. We've built an interconnected world on layers of aging systems, complex configurations, and dependencies that organizations don't always fully understand. A single misconfiguration, failed update, or broken dependency can create disruption on a massive scale, even without an attacker,” Kollender said. “The uncomfortable reality I think we're grappling with is that attackers don't always have to break our systems. Sometimes, our systems are already capable of breaking on their own.” For people who couldn’t withdraw money from their bank, board a flight, or use email at work on Friday, “the disruption was real regardless of the cause,” she said. “Cybersecurity has spent decades investing in detecting threats, identifying vulnerabilities, and generating reports,” according to Kollender. “Yet we still allow for these preventable weaknesses and configurations that can bring entire systems down.” Cynthia Kaiser, senior VP of Halcyon’s Ransomware Research Center and former deputy director of the FBI’s Cyber Division, told The Reg that the recent disruptions show “how deeply interconnected our digital infrastructure has become, and how a single technical failure or software update can cascade with outsized effects across critical systems.” AI has entered the chat Then we go and add AI to this already delicate balance, and everything essentially blows up. AI-assisted bug hunting and exploit development has surfaced more than 100,000 CVEs so far this year, with Microsoft’s Patch Tuesday disclosing more than 1,000 vulnerabilities in each of the past two months. AI has also shrunk the elapsed time between the public release of a security patch and attackers developing working exploits. “We are in an era where AI is accelerating the discovery of legacy software flaws, forcing organizations to race to patch vulnerabilities before adversaries can exploit them, which inevitably creates friction and disruptions,” Kaiser said. “Even when an outage isn’t caused by a cyberattack, these moments of operational distraction leave dangerous gaps open for threat actors and opportunists to take advantage of, making it crucial for both institutions and everyday individuals to remain on high alert against social engineering and unsolicited outreach.” Even when attackers aren’t using AI to facilitate intrusions, the technology itself has become a source of risk to organizations. “Autonomous agents can execute actions, change configurations, access sensitive information, and interact with critical systems at machine speed,” Kollender said. “When those systems lack proper governance and safeguards, a mistake can develop just as quickly as an attack. Former US Department of Defense network exploitation and vulnerability analyst Mike Wiacek, when asked if these regular system outages are the new normal, told us: “The brutal truth is yes. Especially in the AI world that we live in.” After the DoD, Wiacek founded Google’s Threat Analysis Group. He's since founded Stairwell, a threat-intel firm he serves as chief technology officer. “The idea that we are going to patch ourselves to security is, dare I say, an antiquated concept,” he told The Register. One of Stairwell’s engineers was doing regular, daily software development tasks on an open source library with Anthropic’s Claude Mythos, and the model told the engineer about a buffer-overflow vulnerability in the code. “We weren't even looking for it,” Wiacek said. “It found a vulnerability in open source software by accident. You used to need specialized bug hunters and really, really technical security folks to discover and develop vulnerabilities and exploits. Now, it’s almost too easy to do it.” This new reality, he said, necessitates a total rethink of how we build and maintain digital infrastructure. “How do we get to a world where we assume compromised by default, and continuously recompromised, and then develop the architectures and the systems necessary to make what was the expense of incident-response investigation really fast and cheap? Because we will not be able to patch our way out of it.” It requires vulnerability managers and system administrators to patch as soon as software updates become available. But from an engineering perspective, it also means building in “as many fail-safes as possible,” Wiacek said. “An elevator doesn't have just one cable hoisting it,” he continued. “There's a lot of redundancy in those systems. Enterprises and organizations and governments haven't really had to operate like that. But that's going to be the new norm, whether we want it to be or not. Pandora's box is opened, and it's not going to go back inside.” ®

> Hundreds of websites using the Optimizely website personalization platform served unsuspecting visitors a potent malware cocktail that targeted cryptocurrency wallets, stole payment card data, cookies, and screenshots, and delivered exploit kits for infecting iPhones and iPads, researchers said Tuesday.
> ReportURI
> said
> it identified 178 websites—including CNN, Zoom, the BBC, and Salesforce—that were affected. JavaScript digitally signed by Optimizely and then loaded into customer pages had been modified to include malicious components that attempted to infect visitor devices with multiple payloads. When wares were installed successfully, they swapped user cryptocurrency wallet addresses for the attackers. Other components skimmed payment cards, stole cookies and screenshots, and, on iPhones and iPads, delivered iOS exploit kits known as Coruna and DarkSword.
> Optimizely infrastructure delivers multipurpose malware
> Optimizely serves JavaScript “snippets” that include both company code and code that is provided by each customer. The JavaScript, which can be served directly from Optimizely or from a customer endpoint, runs on every page the customer serves. Somehow, the attackers wrote their own code into a portion of each affected customer’s JavaScript and then delivered it from cdn.optimizely.com. A valid certificate for that domain signed the JavaScript.

> 最近遇到一个选择，有点纠结，想问问大家的意见。
>
> 本人江苏大学软件工程专业，27 届，目前在杭州实习，主要做 Java 开发，实习工资 5000 左右。之前了解到转正后薪资可能有 1.5W，但目前还没确定有没有 HC，也没有明确的转正时间。
>
> 前几天拿到了斯堪尼亚南通的实习 Offer，130 一天，另外每天 15 块餐补。岗位主要是制造业 IT 相关的工作，和生产部门、IT 团队一起处理生产过程中遇到的信息系统和技术问题。
>
> 斯堪尼亚的平台肯定是不错的，其实主要是因为它是国际大厂的缘故，不然我连考虑都不带考虑的，根据他这个待遇水平和给的转正回复。。。但现在有个比较大的问题：HR 说今年是第一批采用这种实习招聘模式，以前的实习生一般有机会直接拿正式 Offer，但今年因为市场和预算原因，先招实习生，后面能不能转正还得看 HC。换句话说，表现好也不一定有转正名额。
>
> 我现在最纠结的就是这个。杭州这边虽然也没给我明确承诺，但毕竟已经实习了一段时间，至少还有机会争取一下。万一我为了斯堪尼亚放弃杭州，去了之后又因为没有 HC 转不了正，那不就两头空了吗？
>
> 但反过来想，杭州这边也可能只是我自己觉得有希望，最后同样转不了正。现在就是两个机会都不确定，一个是已经在做的 Java 开发，另一个是平台不错但转正情况不明的外企制造业 IT 岗位。
>
> 想问问大家，如果是你们，会怎么选？
>
> 尤其想听听有制造业 IT、外企或者 Java 开发相关经验的朋友的看法。斯堪尼亚这种经历，对应届生以后找工作到底有多大帮助？值得冒这个转正风险吗？

### [Skill Stow：一个尽量做得清晰、顺手的 macOS AI Skill 管理器](https://www.v2ex.com/t/1258109)

`v2ex:create` · T2 · 2026-11-18 13:14 UTC · zh-CN · by dbaazz · 💬 4

> 平时用 Claude Code、Codex、Cursor、Gemini CLI 这些工具多了，本地 `~/.claude`、`~/.codex`、`~/.cursor` 和各个项目里的 Skill 目录很容易越堆越乱。 其实市面上已经有现成的 Skill 管理器了，功能上大家也都大差不差。我自己又重写一个 **Skill Stow**，主要出发点不是"发明什么新功能"，而是想做一款**自己每天打开…

> 來源提供的正文:
> 平时用 Claude Code、Codex、Cursor、Gemini CLI 这些工具多了，本地 `~/.claude`、`~/.codex`、`~/.cursor` 和各个项目里的 Skill 目录很容易越堆越乱。
>
> 其实市面上已经有现成的 Skill 管理器了，功能上大家也都大差不差。我自己又重写一个 **Skill Stow**，主要出发点不是"发明什么新功能"，而是想做一款**自己每天打开都觉得舒服**的工具：
>
> 1. **信息足够清晰**：哪个 Skill 装在公共库、哪个是某个 Agent 独有、哪个只在当前项目生效，一眼就能看明白，不要一打开全是噪音。
> 2. **交互逻辑顺直**：尽量按桌面端直觉走，减少莫名其妙的跳转和割裂感。
> 3. **UI 和动效细节**：基于 **Go + MyGo** 做的 macOS 原生界面（不是 Web 套壳），在排版、配色（支持浅色/深色）、过渡动画和快捷键上花了不少时间打磨。
>
> ### 顺便带过一下核心能力
>
> - **统一视图**：扫描本机 32 个常见 Agent 目录和项目历史，支持卡片 / 按 Agent 分列看板两种视图。
> - **按 Agent 开关**：直接开关 Claude Code / Codex / Gemini CLI / OpenCode / ZCode 的配置，或软链到其他 Agent。
> - **导入与本地安全检查**：支持 GitHub 链接、`npx skills add` 命令、本地文件夹 / `.zip` 拖入；导入前会先做一遍本地离线扫描（并展示 skills.sh 审计结果）。
> - **可控更新与整理**：GitHub 来源的 Skill 支持看 file-by-file diff 再更新，默认保留旧版到废纸篓；支持一键合并重复副本、对比差异、清理失效软链。
> - **使用统计 & 原生体验**：读取本地 Claude Code / Codex 日志看调用频率；支持 `⌘K` 全局搜索（中文支持拼音）、磁盘实时监听、`⌘Z` 撤销删除。
>
> ### 下载与开源地址
>
> - GitHub：https://github.com/DBAAZzz/skill-stow
> - Release 下载：https://github.com/DBAAZzz/skill-stow/releases/latest
> - 演示视频：（这里可以贴你刚传好的 YouTube 链接）
>
> **说明**：
>
> - **MIT 开源免费**，纯本地运行，无账号、无遥测。
> - 支持 **macOS 12+**（Universal 包，Apple Silicon / Intel 通用）。
> - 目前还没有 Apple Developer ID 签名，首次打开如果被 Gatekeeper 拦截，在「系统设置 -> 隐私与安全性」里点「仍要打开」，或看下 README 里的 `xattr` 放行命令即可。
>
> 做这个项目的初衷就是自己用着顺手，顺便开源出来，欢迎提 Issue 或聊聊交互上的建议。
>

`v2ex:jobs` · T2 · 2026-11-18 06:09 UTC · zh-CN · by sxw · 💬 2

> Microsoft Search Infra team，我们负责微软内部使用的大规模 AI 在线推理平台。我们正在在线系统的运维中使用 AI Agent。它调取日志、监控、部署与配置等多源数据完成问题诊断。积累了数百个真实生产问题，有完整的排查轨迹、评审结果和标注，这为 Agent 的评估与自我进化研究提供了真实的场景和数据。 我们重点关注以下前沿方向： - **Agent 自我进化**：模型权重…

> 來源提供的正文:
> Microsoft Search Infra team，我们负责微软内部使用的大规模 AI 在线推理平台。我们正在在线系统的运维中使用 AI Agent。它调取日志、监控、部署与配置等多源数据完成问题诊断。积累了数百个真实生产问题，有完整的排查轨迹、评审结果和标注，这为 Agent 的评估与自我进化研究提供了真实的场景和数据。
>
> 我们重点关注以下前沿方向：
>
> - **Agent 自我进化**：模型权重不变，让 Agent 从自身经验中自动优化外围系统（Harness），包括提示、技能、工具与记忆，代表工作如 Google Harness²、Meta-Harness、Agentic Harness Engineering
> - **递归自我改进**：Agent 不仅改进自己，也改进"改进的方法"，代表工作如 Darwin Gödel Machine、Hyperagents、AlphaEvolve
> - **经验学习与上下文工程**：从成功和失败的经验中持续沉淀可复用的策略与技能，代表工作如 ACE、ReasoningBank、SkillOpt
> - **Agent 效果评估**：Agent-as-a-Judge、过程级评估，以及检验自我进化是否可靠、能否泛化、成本几何
>
> ## 岗位职责
>
> 这个岗位要做两件事：**让我们的 Agent 的效果能被准确衡量，并让它能根据历史表现自动改进。**
>
> 实习期间，你将有机会参与以下部分工作：
>
> 1. **搭建评测集**：从历史 oncall 问题中整理一套评测集，和 oncall 工程师一起确认每个问题的正确结论、关键证据和合理的排查终点。同时把问题发生时的现场数据固定下来，保证同一个问题可以反复重跑，并且每次结果之间可以比较。
> 2. **开发评测工具**：实现"一条命令跑完整套评测"。指定一个 Agent 版本后，每个问题重复运行多次，输出准确率、结果稳定性、耗时和调用成本；还要能逐题对比两个版本，列出哪些题变好了、哪些题变差了。
> 3. **校准评审 Agent**：对比评审 Agent 的打分和工程师的判断，量化两者的一致程度，找出它容易误判的情况（例如把缺乏证据支持的结论判为可信）。在此基础上改进评审方式，让它的分数可以当作可靠的自动指标来用。
> 4. **实现自动改进流程**：
>    - 自动分析失败的排查记录，归类失败原因，例如漏查了某个数据源、停在表面现象没有追到根因、工具用错等；
>    - 根据失败原因，自动生成对 Agent 的修改，包括调查指引、排查技能文档、工具使用说明和经验库；
>    - 在评测集上验证这些修改，只保留整体有提升、并且没有让原本能解决的问题变差的修改。
> 5. **上线与复盘**：把验证通过的改进合入正式 Agent，跟踪它在真实问题上的效果，并定期整理实验结论与团队分享。
>
> ## 任职要求
>
> 1. 计算机相关专业本科及以上在校学生
> 2. 熟悉 Python 或至少一种编程语言
> 3. 熟悉大模型及 AI Agent
> 4. 熟练使用 AI 编程工具进行开发
> 5. 能阅读英文论文，并动手复现或通过实验验证想法
> 6. 好奇心强、学习能力强，能独立推进问题
> 7. 每周至少到岗实习 3 天，实习期至少 5 个月（可酌情放宽）
>
> ## 加分项
>
> - 有 LLM-as-a-Judge、Benchmark 或评测集构建经验
> - 有相关论文发表或开源项目
>
> ## 你将获得
>
> - 在微软大规模 AI 在线推理平台上，参与生产级 AI Agent 的前沿研究
> - 与一线 oncall 工程师直接合作，接触真实生产问题
> - 完整经历 Agent 从评测、改进到上线的全过程
> - 改进直接合入正式 Agent，对 oncall 效率产生可衡量的影响
> - 充足的模型调用额度（公司提供 GitHub Copilot subscription）
>
> ## 实习信息
>
> - 工作地点：北京市海淀区 丹棱街五号微软大厦
> - 到岗时间：近几个月内可到岗
> - 投递方式：简历请发送至 sunxiaowen@microsoft.com

>
> 1. **TradingView 的 Bar Replay 不能保存回放记录。** 最大问题是关掉页面，上周练的 50 笔单子、撤掉的限价单、当时的胜率和回撤曲线全都没有了，没法跨周对比复盘。
> 2. **主流专业回测平台对只做期货的人太贵、也太重。** 像 FX Replay 要上到 $35/月的 Pro 才给 CME 期货数据；TradeZella $35/月起，核心卖点是 500+ 券商的实盘自动同步和 AI 日志；NinjaTrader Market Replay 只能在 Windows 上按日期手动下载 Replay 数据包；Tradovate Market Replay 单独开通要 $49/月，而且回放图表不是连续合约，每次换日期还得自己翻对应月份的合约代码。
>
>
> 所以我自己写了 **Charts Replay**（[https://chartsreplay.app](https://chartsreplay.app)）。
>
> ---
>
> ## 里面都有哪些标的和数据
>
> 所有期货数据均为**未做向后价差调整的真实成交价**，包含完整电子交易时段（盘前盘后、亚盘、欧盘都在）：
>
> - **ES（E-mini 标普 500）**：2016-01-03 至 2026-11-01，381 万根 1 分钟 K 线（78 个月度合约按成交量切换拼接，0.25 点最小跳动校验）
> - **NQ（E-mini 纳斯达克 100）**：2016-01-03 至 2026-11-01，379 万根 1 分钟 K 线（44 个季度合约按成交量切换拼接，0.25 点最小跳动校验）
> - **GC（COMEX 黄金）**：2016-01-03 至 2026-11-01，378 万根 1 分钟 K 线（55 段主力合约按前一交易日成交量排名拼接，0.10 点最小跳动校验）
> - **BTC/USDT、ETH/USDT 现货**：2017-09-01 至 2026-11-01，分别为 481 万、479 万根 1 分钟 K 线，24/7 连续行情
> - **微型期货（MES / MNQ / MGC）**：和 ES、NQ、GC 价格走势完全一致；在考核模式 `CR FLEX 50K` 里可以直接切到 Micro 模式（40 手上限、原生的微型点值和手续费）
>
> ---
>
> ## 核心功能
>
> ### 1. 按 1 分钟底层撮合的图表回放
> - 支持 1m / 3m / 5m / 15m / 30m / 1h / 4h / 1D 自由切换，播放速度 `1×` 到 `20×`，也可以手动一根一根往前推。
> - 支持**每天固定时段回放**（比如只练纽约时间 `09:30–11:30`），当天窗口走完直接跳到下一个交易日，适合批量刷开盘区间突破（ORB）或 Silver Bullet。
> - 无论当前看什么周期，挂单都会在绘制前先按 **1 分钟 K 线**逐根撮合：限价单触价成交、止损单破价成交、跳空按开盘价处理；同一根 1 分钟 K 线里止损和止盈同时在区间内时，**先撮合止损、再撮合限价**，不给回测留侥幸空间。
>
> ### 2. 完整订单留存与复盘报告
> - 每笔**下单、成交、撤单**（包括从未成交的挂单）都会随会话保存在云端。
> - 图表上的画线按时间和价格存储，15m 画的区间切到 1m 位置完全一致，关闭浏览器或换电脑登录都在。
> - 每个会话自动生成报告：净盈亏、胜率、盈利因子、盈亏比、最大回撤、权益曲线、交易日历，以及每笔交易的持仓时长和 **MAE / MFE**（最大不利/有利变动）。
>
> ### 3. R 值计分的「每日挑战」与 `CR FLEX 50K` 考核模拟
> - **每日挑战（Daily Challenge）**：每天全站玩家拿到同一个匿名的 ES 或 NQ 历史交易日（`09:30–16:00 ET`），固定 `$100,000` 账户、每笔进场强制带止损止盈括号单、单笔风险不能超过余额，按 **R 倍数**（净盈亏 ÷ 承担的总风险）计分上榜；另外还有不限次数的随机一题。
> - **`CR FLEX 50K` 模拟考核账户**：`$50,000` 起步、`+$3,000` 目标、`$2,000` 收盘移动回撤（锁在 `$50,100`）、`40%` 一致性规则、4 手标准合约（或 40 手微型合约）上限、`16:45 ET` 强平。用来在花钱考真实 Prop Firm 之前先磨纪律。
>
> ### 4. 内置两套跟随回放时钟的指标（无前视、不重绘）
> - **`PA Base Indicators`**：按 IBS（Internal Bar Strength）给 K 线分强/中/弱三档着色、RTH 开盘 K 线编号计数、未回补缺口与测量型缺口阴影、高开/低开标识、放量突破失败箭头。
> - **`ICT Base Indicators`**：亚盘/伦敦/纽约时段框、`09:30` 开盘 K 线高亮、15m 至月线多周期 FVG、确认过的流动性高低点（BL/SL）及 `PDH/PDL` 等。高周期区域严格只读取回放时刻已收盘的 K 线。
>
> ---
>
> ## 价格
>
> **免费试用**：Google 或 Discord 登录即送 **7 天完整权限**，不用绑银行卡，会员到期不续费后只会变为只读状态，之前所有记录全部保留。
>
> ---
>
> 欢迎直接来试用，有哪里顺手或不顺手的地方，欢迎评论区或者进 Discord 告诉我：

> - 官网：[https://chartsreplay.app](https://chartsreplay.app)
> - Discord 社区：[https://discord.gg/uKkA3wJQDm](https://discord.gg/uKkA3wJQDm)

> 來源提供的正文:
> 大家好，最近做了个 Mac 小工具，叫「淡出」（DockQuit），想来分享一下，也听听大家的意见。
>
> 它解决的是一个很小的问题：不用打开 Dock 的右键菜单，就能退出正在运行的应用。不替换原生 Dock，也不是强退或清理内存工具。
>
> ### 两种手动操作，都是免费的
>
> - 鼠标停在应用图标上，点出现的 ×。
> - 用鼠标中键点击应用图标。
>
> 它发出的是正常退出请求，未保存内容仍由应用自己提示，不会替你点「不保存」，也不会在退出失败后升级为强退。
>
> 如果操作的是 Dock 中单独显示的最小化窗口缩略图，则会先还原，再关闭那一个窗口，而不是退出整个应用。收进应用图标里的窗口和浏览器标签页不在这个范围内。
>
> ![淡出设置：悬停 ×、鼠标中键和可选自动退出](https://dockquit.heino.top/assets/screenshots/settings-zh-light-20261118.webp)
>
> ### 还有一个可选的自动退出
>
> 可以给指定应用开启：当它已经没有窗口，并且你切换到其他应用后，再请求正常退出。等待时间可以选立即、15、30 或 60 秒；「立即」也要先切走并完成检查，不是一关窗口就退出。
>
> 隐藏、最小化不算关窗。没有窗口也不代表没有后台任务，所以播放音乐、下载、编译这类应用，需要谨慎选择。
>
> 这一项可以在 App 内主动开启 7 天试用，中国大陆目前标价 29 元一次买断，税费和最终总额以结账为准。试用不会自动扣款，到期后手动退出和单窗口操作仍然免费。
>
> 给 V 友准备了 Auto-quit 的五折早鸟优惠码，需要的话在评论区留个言就可以领取。手动功能本身免费，不需要优惠码。
>
> ![淡出自动退出设置：选择应用和等待时间](https://dockquit.heino.top/assets/screenshots/autoQuit-zh-light-20261118.webp)
>
> ### 安装和下载
>
> 需要开启辅助功能权限。官网提供 Developer ID 签名并公证的 DMG，系统要求 macOS 14+，提供 Universal 安装包。
>
> 官网和下载：[淡出 DockQuit](https://dockquit.heino.top/zh/)
>
> 如果你已经习惯 Command-Q，可能不需要它；如果更习惯用鼠标在 Dock 上处理应用，可以试试看。
>
> 也想听听大家的具体反馈：悬停 × 和中键哪种更顺手？应用退出与单窗口关闭会不会容易混淆？如果遇到误触、识别不准或不该退出的情况，也欢迎告诉我对应应用和系统版本。谢谢。

`v2ex:create` · T2 · 2026-11-18 15:06 UTC · zh-CN · by daqzi

> 最近在折腾 Sub2API 的账号池，做了个模型质量巡检工具，分享给有同样需求的佬友。 一个分组里挂了好几个上游账号，接口都能正常返回，但有的账号碰到同一道题就是答不好。我想做的是让 Sub2API 自己定时出题、记录结果，发现异常就先把那个账号移出调度，等复测过了再放回来。 可以直接嵌进 Sub2API 巡检服务用 Docker Compose 单独部署，连上已有的 Sub2API，再加一个自定…

> 來源提供的正文:
> 最近在折腾 Sub2API 的账号池，做了个模型质量巡检工具，分享给有同样需求的佬友。
>
> 一个分组里挂了好几个上游账号，接口都能正常返回，但有的账号碰到同一道题就是答不好。我想做的是让 Sub2API 自己定时出题、记录结果，发现异常就先把那个账号移出调度，等复测过了再放回来。
> 可以直接嵌进 Sub2API
> 巡检服务用 Docker Compose 单独部署，连上已有的 Sub2API，再加一个自定义菜单，就能在原来的面板里打开巡检页面。沿用 Sub2API 登录，无需改网关源码。 管理员可以配置巡检，普通用户也能选自己的 Key 测一轮。
> 自动剔除后，怎么恢复？
> 举个例子，给一个分组设成每小时巡检一次，选一道逻辑题和一道 JSON 题。如果某个账号明确答错了标准答案题，开启自动剔除后，巡检就会暂时停用这个账号的调度。
>
> 冷却结束后，系统会单独复测原账号。这时候账号还在暂停调度，全部复测题通过才会恢复接单。 如果没通过，就继续冷却。遇到超时、限额之类的请求问题，巡检可以按优先级换同组账号，结果也会单独记录。
>
> 自动剔除默认关闭，可以先跑几轮看看结果，再决定要不要开。
> 能测哪些题？
> 内置了糖果题、逻辑选择题、数值计算、JSON 指令遵循、指纹观察、鹈鹕骑自行车。每个分组可以多选题目，还能改题干、标准答案和每题请求次数。
>
> 有标准答案的题可以自动判。像「鹈鹕骑自行车」这类题，可以直接在结果页看 SVG 作品，也能翻历史，把不同时间的回答放在一起看。单轮答错适合当排查线索，判断模型表现有多稳定，可以多看几轮。
>
> 项目基于 NoonWake.AI 的 AI Drool Router 二次开发。欢迎佬友试用，尤其想听听大家平时都用什么题来测模型，或者希望巡检遇到什么情况时自动暂停账号。项目地址
> https://github.com/daQzi/code1024-drool-router

> 它比较适合想把英语练习放进日常键盘输入里的朋友：选一门课程，先看着英文跟打，熟悉后切换到听写或中译英，检查自己能不能把内容还原出来。练过的词句可以从学习记录按日期找回，优先回看错误较多、还不熟悉的内容。
>
> 比如 `I usually walk to work.` 这样的短句，可以先理解句意，再跟打；之后听音频输入，看看自己是漏了词、拼错了 usually，还是对语序不熟。这是练法示例，重点是发现具体卡在哪里。
>
> **和 Qwerty Learner、句乐部怎么选？**
>
> 按目前的官方功能说明，可以先看自己的练习目标：
>
> - **Qwerty Learner**：如果主要想按考试词库、程序员词库练单词拼写和默写，可以先试它。项目开源，在线版能直接进入练习。
> - **句乐部**：如果喜欢从单词、语块逐步练到整句，或比较需要 AI 讲解、自动复习安排和多种材料形式，可以了解它。
> - **HappyTapper**：如果想选课程做跟打、听写和中译英，再自主找回练过的词句，比较推荐试试。它的日期回看会按错误和熟悉度排序，下一次什么时候复习由自己安排。
>
> **使用门槛**
>
> HappyTapper 的实际课程练习需要登录，免费版每天最多 50 个练习项，可以先试试练习流程是否适合自己，有需要再考虑专业版。
>
> 网站上也有更详细的工具选型说明：
> https://www.happytapper.app/docs/typing-english-tools
>
> 上面的对比基于公开功能说明，供选工具时参考。打字练习之外，阅读、听力和真实交流也需要继续。
>
> 有用过这几款工具的朋友吗？你更在意词库和拼写、句子的提示与讲解，还是练完以后怎么复习？

>
> 包括但不限于 家庭组、ACP（或其他）反代、免费薅Pro 的方法来获取Google AI Pro以及将Gemini 4额度反代出来的方式基本被谷歌逐一处理了。甚至有佬在反重力里正常使用也出现被封禁的情况——加之反重力封了一次之后可以出狱，但是再进宫就彻底废掉的现象，加之目前的市场，可以做几点总结。
>
> https://linux.do#p-24948056-h-1-21. 谷歌加大了对所有反代的封禁力度，而且封禁几乎具有不可逆性。
>
> 反重力里正常使用都可能会被封禁（ACP不用说跑不了）+二进宫必死决定了谷歌处理的力度相对较大。
>
> AIStudio前段时间频发验证+封AIStudio后有概率直接杀号，也是相当大力度的处理。
>
> 家庭组连坐现在发生的频率变高了很多。
>

>
> 空手套白狼，或者潮水一样的不对等的薅羊毛形式可能将更为稀有（甚至绝迹了）
>
> 目前Jio/学生优惠之类的Pro已经无法使用Gemini 4.
>
> 而复活的Pixel渠道和Xiaomi相对的有着Gemini 4的访问权限，但是市场价也更加昂贵。基本10元往上
>
> 而接下来的档位则是付费Pro，最便宜的是日区/新区+学生优惠，在4年时间里月费可以削减到约30RMB的价格。同时也拥有Hydrogen/Argon的访问权限——以及Colab的200点数——最为完整的Pro权益。
>
> 再接下来是Ultra，已经经历了0元购清洗+低价区下车。而本身也享有最高的权益，也就是Cabon、Neon（以及未来所有可能的Gemini顶级模型的首发享受权益），其它的量更大不必说。

### [比jev快一倍、便宜20%，还开源？MachinePulseAI 开源多模态决策模型 Karpo Decision 31B，登顶Hugging Face Decision Index 第一名](https://linux.do/t/topic/3200074)

`linuxdo:前沿快讯` · T2 · 2026-11-18 18:25 UTC · zh-CN · by Davidddd

> 佬们，MachinePulseAI刚刚发布的原生多模态决策模型系列Karpo Decision 31B，同时还开源了0.8B、2B、4B、9B、12B五个不同参数量的模型
>
> 先放链接：
>
> Hugging Face 模型权重：
>
> [huggingface.co](https://huggingface.co/MachinePulseAI/karpo-decision-31B)
>
> ![](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/f/2/1/f21fc01487f92db4d4f28bf6041b90cb6930077d_2_690x372.png)
>
> [MachinePulseAI/karpo-decision-31B · Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/MachinePulseAI/karpo-decision-31B)
>
> Text Classification model with 31B parameters. Download, explore files and run it on Hugging Face.
>
> 官方中文技术博客
>
> ![](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/a/e/f/aef4341fbbbd55bd179d8e1ff303461860b41dd2.png)
> [karpo.ai](https://karpo.ai/zh/models/decision)
>
> [Karpo Decision：一次前向推理，读出全部答案](https://karpo.ai/zh/models/decision)
>
> 给 agent 用的决策模型。给它一个状态和几个带类型的问题，它返回每个问题每个选项的概率，不生成任何 token。
>
> [![image](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/c/5/d/c5d7dba308d7ca67a37b8f5496e195bbf3ad5ae5_2_690x327.jpeg)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/c/5/d/c5d7dba308d7ca67a37b8f5496e195bbf3ad5ae5.jpeg)
>
> 榜单：
>
> [huggingface.co](https://huggingface.co/spaces/multimodalart/jev-decision-index)
>
> ![](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/2/f/e/2fe9e5544c769676fb6dc8eb8a912da00fed8e18_2_690x362.png)
>
> [Jev Decision Index - a Hugging Face Space by multimodalart](https://huggingface.co/spaces/multimodalart/jev-decision-index)
>
> Benchmarks and news on various repros of TypeSafe's Jev
>
> 这个模型直接冲上了 Decision Index 0.4.1 Full 榜单的 #1（在 300 个模型中拿到了 73.9 分），
>
> 在多项 Agent 核心指标上击败各大厂的闭源模型（Gemini Decision 1、TypeSafe Jev 1.14 和OpenAI GPT-6 Luna）
>
> https://linux.do#p-24947675-h-1以防不知道：啥是决策模型？
>
> Agent每走一步，背后其实都是一连串高频的【小判断】
>
> 比如：
>
> 当前网页该点哪个按钮？
>
> 这个商品满足用户需求吗？
>
> 现在该调工具还是停下来追问用户？
>
> 这些活能让传统的大模型干，但是有四个缺点：
>
> 慢：必须逐个 token 解码生成，往往还要先跑一段 CoT 思考，一个简单判断动辄几百毫秒到几秒
>
> 贵：每次判断都要走完整的生成调用
>
> 输出不可控：需要写正则从文本里抠答案，模型甚至可能抽风生成不在选项里的内容
>
> 没有可信的置信度：没有经过校准的概率分布，工程上根本没法量化一个阈值，到底啥时候让agent做什么具体的任务
>
> 所以Jev来了，typesafe在9月15日发布Jev决策模型：给它当前情况、一个问题和几个候选动作，它会判断该选哪个，并返回各选项的概率
>
> e.g. 客服收到退货申请后，它可以根据订单和退货政策，在这四个选项中做选择
>
> A:同意退款
>
> B:拒绝
>
> C:补充信息
>
> D:转人工
>
> 与生成长篇回答的聊天模型不同，这类模型专注于快速判断，适合用来决定 AI Agent 下一步该做什么
>
> 然后这些大厂也没掉队，各自都发布了他们自己的决策模型，比如Google前几天刚发布的Gemini Decision，还有微软的Microsoft-Decision-1
>
> [![asynccode](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/3/8/a/38a0cc59ecac2e0a6b3f0f749d06496d6c78816b_2_569x500.png)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/3/8/a/38a0cc59ecac2e0a6b3f0f749d06496d6c78816b.png)
>
> [![asynccode](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/6/3/0/63059838a1f0900b3233f7ca608e43e05d48a0ab_2_689x500.png)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/6/3/0/63059838a1f0900b3233f7ca608e43e05d48a0ab.png)
>
> 然后hugging face专门做了一个decision index的排行榜，用一系列的benchmark来给这些决策模型打分
>
> 它关注模型能否根据给定信息做出正确选择，比如该调用哪个工具、是否需要追问用户，或者网页上该点哪个按钮，评测包含公开测试和私有测试，既看模型在熟悉任务上的表现，也看它能否应对新领域
>
> 榜单链接在：
>
> [huggingface.co](https://huggingface.co/spaces/multimodalart/jev-decision-index)
>
> ![](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/2/f/e/2fe9e5544c769676fb6dc8eb8a912da00fed8e18_2_690x362.png)
>
> [Jev Decision Index - a Hugging Face Space by multimodalart](https://huggingface.co/spaces/multimodalart/jev-decision-index)
>
> Benchmarks and news on various repros of TypeSafe's Jev
>
> 最近，Karpo Decision登上了榜首，它还是一个开源模型，居然能吊打这些大厂的闭源模型
>
> [![image](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/c/f/4/cf4a5cb4c72c6ffc711b00d847cf58a20796a34f_2_690x230.jpeg)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/c/f/4/cf4a5cb4c72c6ffc711b00d847cf58a20796a34f.jpeg)
>
> https://linux.do#p-24947675-benchmark-2benchmark
>
> [![image](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/c/5/d/c5d7dba308d7ca67a37b8f5496e195bbf3ad5ae5_2_690x327.jpeg)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/c/5/d/c5d7dba308d7ca67a37b8f5496e195bbf3ad5ae5.jpeg)
>
> Decision Index 登顶#1：在 Decision Index 维护方用私有测试集（60% 同技能 + 40% 全新领域）跑出的 Full 榜上拿到 73.9分，位列 300 个模型之首
>
> （作为对比，闭源标杆 Jev 1.14 的 Full 分为 60.2）
>
> 正面硬刚商业闭源 API：在 personal agent 最常做的三类高频判断上，全面领先 Google 的 Gemini Decision 1、Jev 1.14 和 GPT-6 Luna：
>
> When2Call（何时调工具/追问）：90.4%对比 Gemini Decision 1 的 79.9%、Jev 1.14 的 82.0%、GPT-6 Luna 的 70.4%
>
> Mind2Web Multimodal（多模态网页元素点击）：90.0%（对比 Gemini 86.2%、Jev 86.8%）
>
> Amazon ESCI（电商商品匹配细粒度分类 Macro-F1）：64.7%（对比 Gemini 58.7%、Jev 56.7%）
>
> [![image](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/c/6/e/c6e0bd95ac8184c75ecc67e5a86457d7fa548558_2_690x325.png)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/c/6/e/c6e0bd95ac8184c75ecc67e5a86457d7fa548558.png)
>
> WildGuardTest（安全审核）：平均准确率 93.4%，同样位居榜首。
>
> 单卡即可部署：单张 RTX PRO 6000可跑31B，接口直接兼容 System One API。在公开集 14 万+ 请求上，bf16 中位延迟仅95 ms；开启团队优化的 FP8 + CUDA Graph + Triton Global Attention后，中位延迟进一步压到73 ms，吞吐高达 7,100 tok/s，峰值显存从 80 GB 降到约60GB且精度零损
>
> 原生多模态 + 256k 长上下文：基于 Gemma 4 31B微调，原生支持直接传入图片和文本共同判断；默认支持 32k 序列，最高支持 256k 上下文，超过 32k 会自动带完整共享内容分段，绝不悄悄截断
>
> 0.8B \~ 31B 全家桶开源：除了31B，y一共放出0.8B、2B、4B、9B、12B五个轻量尺寸，小显存机器也能跑
>
> 在防刷榜的私有题库里，公开榜前十名的模型一旦进入同技能私有盲测，成绩平均要暴跌6.8分，唯独Karpo只掉了4.3分，在前十名里抗跌能力最强，到了全新领域私有题上更是拿下78.6分
>
> [![asynccode](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/2/c/6/2c63e319bed06526fb9d0ac615c9431add981d85_2_690x390.png)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/2/c/6/2c63e319bed06526fb9d0ac615c9431add981d85.png)
>
> 同时，它也把KnowLine、GLiDE、Sieve等原榜单前三的开源对手悉数甩在身后
>
> [![asynccode](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/7/6/0/76034df8aebd1f6294d413bbab43961ce785ba08_2_690x496.png)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/7/6/0/76034df8aebd1f6294d413bbab43961ce785ba08.png)
>
> 同时，Karpo每千次决策成本仅需$0.025，相当于做4万次判断才花1美元
>
> https://linux.do#p-24947675-h-3官方场景实测
>
> 团队本身在海外深耕本地生活智能体 Karpo 与浏览器智能体 Karpo Browser，官网里有两个有意思的demo：
>
> 10个胃口，一张菜单（916 毫秒配齐 10 人点餐）：
>
> 把整张菜单和 10 位顾客各自的卡路里、预算、过敏原塞进一次请求，916 ms同时配齐 10 道菜，硬约束与软偏好拿满分
>
> ![Screen-Recording-2026-11-19](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/6/9/a/69a40edf5e6d32bdad4d8e9401bf1a7e46011045.gif)
>
> 城市扫描仪：同一个推理请求，交给karpo decision和Gemini 3.5 Flash，看哪个模型先答完
>
> ![Screen-Recording-2026-11-17-17.28.03-compressed](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/8/5/0/850bff898977e3bcdbe55f652df21e47e8e183e5.webp)
>
> 除了这两个案例，佬也可以在官网的playground里面直接试用模型：
>
> ![](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/a/e/f/aef4341fbbbd55bd179d8e1ff303461860b41dd2.png)
> [karpo.ai](https://karpo.ai/zh/models/decision)
>
> [Karpo Decision：一次前向推理，读出全部答案](https://karpo.ai/zh/models/decision)
>
> 给 agent 用的决策模型。给它一个状态和几个带类型的问题，它返回每个问题每个选项的概率，不生成任何 token。
>
> 可以在这里面修改问题和选项，把模型的几大能力都测试一下！
>
> [![image](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/9/3/2/932ebb7a6744079f889744c374145fef23f9537a_2_623x500.png)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/9/3/2/932ebb7a6744079f889744c374145fef23f9537a.png)
>
> https://linux.do#p-24947675-h-4开发者怎么用？
>
> 做Personal Agent、搜索和推荐的开发者，都可以直接把模型接到自己的app里，
>
> 以【帮用户找一家适合聊天的酒馆】这个需求为例：
>
> Personal agent：可以让模型选择下一步动作。像grok bot这样的产品，最难的部分是【面对用户的模糊指令】，可以在工程上先让决策模型判断一下，再把结果作为context一起返回给传统的LLM，比如：先追问用户想去哪一带，还是直接按当前位置调用搜索工具（对应 When2Call 90.4% 的判断力与 0.023 校准误差，把握高直接执行，拿不准主动追问）
>
> 搜索：可以用模型判断每家店和查询有多匹配，利用 Branch Attention 一次并发扫描几十家召回店铺的介绍和评论，在几百毫秒内把“背景音乐轻、方便聊天”的店精准打高分排在前面。
>
> 推荐：可以用模型在符合条件的店里做个性化选择：结合用户画像，让偏爱精酿的人先看到啤酒馆，喜欢自然酒的人先看到葡萄酒吧
>
> 佬们可以带上自己产品的请求和几个候选项，在playground里换成自己的，测试一下模型咋选：
>
> ![](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/a/e/f/aef4341fbbbd55bd179d8e1ff303461860b41dd2.png)

### [终末地B站直播激励连点脚本](https://linux.do/t/topic/3200032)

`linuxdo:开发调优` · T2 · 2026-11-18 17:47 UTC · zh-CN · by Cloud_Sail

> 适用于形式如下的页面：
>
> https://www.bilibili.com/blackboard/era/award-exchange.html?task_id=18ERA1wloghv2ya00
>
> 如果不是终末地的激励可能会有不同，我只保证终末地可用，并且功能尽可能少。
>
> 功能有两个：
>
> 将按钮从button exchange-button disable类改为button exchange-button；
>
> 在限定的时段内，以限定的速度连点（直接调用按钮类的点击方法click()）。
>
> 为了控制和调试，在页面右上角添加一个按钮，能无视设置切换连点的状态。
>
> NOTICE: 若已经通过按钮切换过连点，则不会在时段到达时自动开始连点，需要注意在开抢前刷新一次页面，避免到了时间没开抢。
>
> 现在的设置抢了几次没有被封，如果把间隔时间减到150ms，或者提前开始连点的时间设置到23:59:50的话，可能被封（我就被封了两天）。
>
> ```
> // ==UserScript==
> // @name         B站活动兑换页 - 极简连点
> // @namespace    http://tampermonkey.net/
> // @version      2.1
> // @match        *://*.bilibili.com/blackboard/era/award-exchange.html*
> // @grant        none
> // @run-at       document-idle
> // ==/UserScript==
>
> (function () {
>     'use strict';
>
>     // ====== 配置 ======
>     const SKIP_TEXT  = '查看奖励';
>     const CLICK_GAP  = 200;
>     const TIME_START = '23:59:55'; // HH:mm:ss
>     const TIME_END   = '00:00:15'; // 支持跨天
>     // ==================
>
>     let clicking = false;
>     let clickTimer = null;
>     let is_manual_change = false; // 上一次状态是否由按钮点击导致
>
>     // 'HH:mm:ss' → 当天毫秒数
>     function toMs(str) {
>         const [h, m, s] = str.split(':').map(Number);
>         return ((h * 3600) + (m * 60) + (s || 0)) * 1000;
>     }
>
>     // 当前时间 → 当天毫秒数
>     function nowMs() {
>         const d = new Date();
>         return ((d.getHours() * 3600) + (d.getMinutes() * 60) + d.getSeconds()) * 1000
>              + d.getMilliseconds();
>     }
>
>     // 是否在时间窗口内（start>end 时取反，即跨天）
>     function inWindow() {
>         const now = nowMs(), start = toMs(TIME_START), end = toMs(TIME_END);
>         return start < end
>             ? (now > start && now < end)
>             : (now > start || now < end);
>     }
>
>     function getTarget() {
>         return document.querySelector('div.button.exchange-button');
>     }
>
>     function removeDisable() {
>         const el = getTarget();
>         if (el && el.textContent.trim() !== SKIP_TEXT) {
>             el.classList.remove('disable');
>         }
>     }
>
>     // ---------- 按钮 ----------
>     const btn = document.createElement('button');
>     Object.assign(btn.style, {
>         position: 'fixed', top: '10px', right: '10px', zIndex: 999999,
>         padding: '6px 12px', color: '#fff', border: 'none',
>         borderRadius: '4px', cursor: 'pointer',
>     });
>
>     // 统一渲染：文案 + 颜色 + 连点定时器（幂等，不会重复建）
>     function refresh() {
>         if (clicking) {
>             btn.textContent = '停止连点';
>             btn.style.background = '#fb7299';
>             if (!clickTimer) {
>                 clickTimer = setInterval(() => {
>                     const el = getTarget();
>                     if (!el || el.textContent.trim() === SKIP_TEXT) {
>                         stopClicking();
>                         return;
>                     }
>                     el.click();
>                 }, CLICK_GAP);
>             }
>         } else {
>             btn.textContent = '已停止';
>             btn.style.background = '#999';
>             if (clickTimer) { clearInterval(clickTimer); clickTimer = null; }
>         }
>     }
>
>     function startClicking() { clicking = true; refresh(); }
>     function stopClicking()  { clicking = false; refresh(); }
>
>     // 按钮点击：取反 + 标记手动
>     btn.onclick = () => {
>         is_manual_change = true;
>         clicking = !clicking;
>         refresh();
>     };
>
>     // 定时检查
>     setInterval(() => {
>         removeDisable();
>         if (is_manual_change) return;
>         if (inWindow()) startClicking();
>         else stopClicking();
>     }, 500);
>
>     document.body.appendChild(btn);
>     refresh();
> })();
> ```
>
> AI写的，但是经过我完整审查，不晓得算不算原创。
>
> 顺便一提，经过1.6上半激励折腾，下半的激励已经很少人在做了，如果感兴趣的话，下一期激励可以试一试。

### [【逆向扒皮】导出 5,661 行账单算明白了：智谱老版 V2 根本不是按 Prompt 次数扣费！](https://linux.do/t/topic/3199989)

`linuxdo:开发调优` · T2 · 2026-11-18 17:24 UTC · zh-CN · by whoAmII

> https://linux.do#p-24946981-h-5661-v2-prompt-1m-945-1【逆向扒皮】导出 5,661 行账单算明白了：智谱老版 V2 根本不是按 Prompt 次数扣费！1M 窗口下 94.5% 额度全喂了缓存
>
> 手里一直留着智谱绝版老套餐 GLM Coding Max V2（个人包季，¥422.1/月）。以前 Claude Code 默认锁 200K 窗口的时候觉得还挺耐造，最近放开 1M 上下文 跑多终端项目，体感直接崩盘：
>
> 整整一周，我连 1 次旗舰 GLM-5.3 都没敢开，全程 100% 挂最便宜的 glm-5.3-flash，面板显示 Cache 命中率 94.8%、低峰期占比 92.5%，结果从周四（11-12）刷新算起，撑了不到 5.6 天直接 100% 周限额熔断停机。
>
> 官方文档对老版 V2 的说明一直是：“Max 每周最多约 8,000 次 prompts（每次 prompt 预计可调用模型 15–30 次）”。为了搞清楚为什么连用 Flash 都撑不过一周，我直接去财务后台导出了这周从 0% 跑到 100% 停机的完整费用明细 Excel（共 5,661 行，精确到分钟级结算批次），用脚本逐行跑了一遍逆向审计。
>
> 算完只有一个感受：以前以为老版 V2 是“按次计费、不看 Token”，纯属想多了。它底层就是一个锁死 10 亿基准额度、且对 Cached Tokens 零折扣（1:1 原价硬扣）的原始计数器。 在 1M 长上下文工作流下，这套老算法简直是吞额度的无底洞。
>
> 所有数据均来自本人实付账单脱敏统计，发出来给还在续费老 V2 的兄弟们提个醒。
>
> ---
>
> https://linux.do#p-24946981-h-5661-2一、 样本底数：面板统计与 5,661 行明细对齐
>
> 订阅档位：个人版 GLM Coding Max V2 - 季（月付原价 ¥469，包季 9 折实付 ¥422.1/月，折合 ¥98.5/周）
>
> 采样区间：2026-11-13 08:18 — 2026-11-18 23:25（从 0% 完整跑到 100% 触发限额阻断）
>
> 使用姿势：Claude Code 裸机流（开启 1M 上下文，未装任何吸 Token 的第三方插件/MCP）
>
> 模型占比：5,651 行全为 glm-5.3-flash（GLM-5.3 为 0 行），外加 10 行走独立赠送包抵扣的搜索/网页读取。
>
> 先核对面板汇总数字与 Excel 逐行求和，原始用量记录本身是对得上的：
>
> 原始总 Tokens：2,176,312,018（即 21.76 亿 / 2.18B，除以 7 天正好对应面板日均 310.9M）
>
> 缓存命中：2,060,627,328（20.61 亿，占总输入 94.87%，面板显示 94.8%）
>
> 未命中新输入：111,407,227（1.11 亿，占总 Token 5.12%）
>
> 模型输出：4,277,463（428 万，仅占总 Token 0.20%）
>
> 时段分布：非高峰期 2,014,510,610（20.15 亿，占 92.57%）；工作日 14:00–18:00 高峰期 161,801,408（1.62 亿，仅占 7.43%）。
>
> ---
>
> https://linux.do#p-24946981-h-8000-prompts-3二、 核心扒皮：“8,000 次 Prompts”到底是怎么算出来的？
>
> https://linux.do#p-24946981-h-1-41. 先证伪“按请求次数扣费”
>
> 智谱账单每分钟会把同一批请求的 输入、缓存命中、输出 拆成 3 行记录，请求次数 (仅API) 字段在同批次 3 行中重复出现。按唯一结算批次去重后，全周共 1,892 个批次：
>
> 真实 API 请求总数：10,166 次（闲时 9,454 次 + 高峰 712 次）。
>
> 按官方 V2 规则，glm-5.3-flash 系数为 闲时 0.4x、高峰 1.2x。如果后台真是数请求次数：
> 9,454 \times 0.4 + 712 \times 1.2 = \mathbf{4,636.0\text{ 次}}
>
> 根本对不上：官方标称每周 8,000 次 prompts（按每次调 15–30 次模型算更是高达 12 万～24 万次请求）。就算按最黑的 1 次 API 请求 = 1 次 prompt 硬算，4,636 也才刚过 8,000 的一半（57.95%），绝不可能触发 100% 停机。
>
> https://linux.do#p-24946981-h-2-999966-52. 真正的熔断公式（精确到 99.9966% 撞墙）
>
> 换个思路，把账单里每一行的原始 Token（完全不区分缓存命中、新输入还是输出，三者 1:1 直接相加），乘上 glm-5.3-flash 的峰谷系数：
>
> $$\begin{aligned}
>
> \text{闲时折算消耗} &= 2,014,510,610 \times 0.4 = 805,804,244.0 \
>
> \text{高峰折算消耗} &= 161,801,408 \times 1.2 = 194,161,689.6 \
>
> \text{全周折算总计} &= \mathbf{999,965,933.6}
>
> \end{aligned}$$
>
> 看到 999,965,933.6 这个数的时候直接破案了：
>
> 在 11月18日 23:25 停机前的最后一秒，我的加权消耗刚好卡在 1,000,000,000（整整 10 亿基准池）的 99.9966%，只剩 34,066 基准额度（按 Flash 闲时 0.4x 反推只够发 8.5 万 原始 Token，连我下一轮 20 多万的上下文都发不出去，当场熔断）。
>
> 可能有兄弟会问：既然池子锁死 10 亿（1.0B），你面板上那 2.18B（21.76亿） 是怎么跑出来的？
>
> 很简单：10 亿 是按 1.0x（即旗舰 GLM-5.3 闲时倍率）定的基准池。因为我全程只敢跑 glm-5.3-flash，它在闲时打 4 折（0.4x）——如果 100% 纯闲时跑 Flash，理论封顶能跑 10\text{亿} \div 0.4 = \mathbf{25\text{亿（2.50B）}}；但我混了 7.43%（1.62 亿）的工作日下午高峰（按 1.2x 扣了 1.94 亿池子），剩下的 8.06 亿池子除以 0.4 跑出 20.15 亿，两段加起来 20.15亿 + 1.62亿 = 21.76亿（2.18B），一分不差把 10 亿基准池扣穿！
>
> 再拿这个 10 亿 基准池除以官方宣传的 8,000 次 prompts：
>
> \frac{1,000,000,000}{8,000\text{ prompts}} = \mathbf{125,000\text{ 加权总 Tokens / prompt}}
>
> (5 小时限额同理：200,000,000 \div 1,600\text{ prompts} = 125,000。我这周刚好跑了 7,999.73 个虚拟 prompt 被拉闸。)
>
> 说白了，所谓“8,000 次 prompt”根本不是按交互次数计费，只是智谱拿早年小窗口时期“平均一轮交互消耗 12.5 万总 Token”包装出来的展示单位；一旦你敢切到 GLM-5.3（闲时 1.0x / 高峰 3.0x），整周纯闲时也就 10 亿、下午高峰更是只有 3.33 亿 就会直接见底。
>
> ---
>
> https://linux.do#p-24946981-h-1m-v2-6三、 为什么 1M 窗口下老 V2 变成了“吞金兽”？
>
> 拆开这 10 亿基准池的去向，问题出在三个叠加的机制硬伤上：
>
> https://linux.do#p-24946981-h-1-cached-tokens-11-9449-71. Cached Tokens 零折扣，1:1 原价硬扣（吃掉全周 94.49% 配额）
>
> 做 Agent 开发的老哥都清楚，Claude Code 干活时 90% 以上的输入都是在反复重读前缀上下文（KV Cache 命中）。在正常的按量或积分体系里，缓存命中因为几乎不占算力，单价只有正常输入的 1/10 到 1/50（就连智谱自己 7 月底涨价后的新版 V3 积分制，也把缓存权重降到了输入的约 1/4）。
>
> 但老版 V2 的计数器完全不管缓存与否，缓存命中、新输入、模型输出全部按 1:1:1 等权硬扣：
>
> 我这一周真正产出的 428 万 输出 Token，只占周额度的 0.20%；
>
> 真正新喂进去的 1.11 亿 未命中输入，只占周额度的 5.30%；
>
> 高达 94.49% 的周额度，全被 20.61 亿 重复读取的旧缓存给吞掉了！
>
> 随手拎出我账单里真实的一笔单次请求（11-13 13:21，API 请求次数 = 1）：当时会话攒了 316,352 缓存，这一步只发了 1,229 新输入，模型仅回了 75 个输出 Token。在缓存打折的渠道里这一下几乎不掉血，但在 V2 里直接按 317,656 × 0.4 = 12.7 万 扣走你 1 整个虚拟 prompt（其中 99.59% 都是在为旧聊天记录复读买单）。
>
> https://linux.do#p-24946981-h-2-1m-82. 1M 上下文的滚雪球反噬
>
> 把全周 1,892 个批次按“单次 API 请求携带的平均上下文大小”分段统计（见配图 ③）：
>
> 单次请求上下文区间
> API 请求次数
> 占总请求数比例
> 吞噬周总额度比例
>
> < 100K
> 2,087 次
> 20.5%
> 5.4%
>
> 100K – 200K
> 2,923 次
> 28.8%
> 18.7%
>
> 200K – 300K
> 2,875 次
> 28.3%
> 37.2%
>
> 300K – 450K
> 1,810 次
> 17.8%
> 28.6%
>
> > 450K（最高 708K）
> 471 次
> 4.6%
> 10.1%
>
> 可以看到：超过 200K 的请求数虽然只占了一半（50.7%），却烧掉了全周 75.9% 的配额！ 在 1M 窗口下只要懒得清理会话，挂着三四十万上下文让 Agent 连续调十几次 Read/Bash 查代码，额度直接呈指数级蒸发。
>
> https://linux.do#p-24946981-h-3-14001800-3-93. 下午 14:00–18:00 的 3 倍暴击
>
> 全周我在工作日下午 2 点到 6 点其实只跑了 7.43% 的 Token，但因为 1.2x 是闲时 0.4x 的 3 倍，这点零头直接啃掉了 19.42%（近五分之一） 的周额度。
>
> ---
>
> https://linux.do#p-24946981-agent-10四、 客观横评：现在重度跑 Agent 到底哪家不坑？（无吹无黑）
>
> 既然把手头几家都在用的账单凑齐了，干脆拿我这一周 21.76 亿/周（折合每月约 93.3 亿 Token，94.9% 缓存命中） 的完全相同重度负载做个横向对账，每家的优缺点和暗坑都摆在明面上：
>
> 智谱老版 Max V2（绝版季付 ¥422.1/月）
>
> 唯一真优势：并发极猛。翻看这周账单，我在峰值一分钟内并发打出过 116 次 API 请求，全程没吃过 429 限流，家里同时挂十几个终端跑自动化确实不卡脖子。
>
> 致命硬伤：缓存 1:1 硬扣跟 1M 长窗口天生八字不合；花 400 多一个月连 GLM-5.3 都不敢开，纯当 Flash 苦力卡用性价比已经掉队了。
>
> 智谱新版 V3 积分制（Pro ¥538 / Max ¥1,078）
>
> 现状：修好了缓存折扣（约 2.4 折），但价格直接起飞。把我这周的账单套进新版积分公式，折算消耗 77,794 积分/周——意味着 ¥538/月的 Pro（每周 6 万积分）根本不够跑，想覆盖同等负载得掏 ¥1,078/月 上新版 Max，纯大冤种价。
>
> 阿里百炼个人版 Token Plan（11月提额后：Std ¥139 / Pro ¥312）
>
> 优势：缓存大概按 1 折扣 Credits，不怕挂长上下文；我自己另一台机器实测 18,000 Credits 跑了 8.83 亿 Token（当时缓存命中率 87.7%），提额后单算每元 Token 性价比确实高。
>
> 恶心人的坑点：第一是锁并发（Lite 1-2、Std 3-4、Pro 也才 6-8 并发，多开几个终端再赶上 Claude 自动派生 Subagent 搜代码，很容易撞 429 排队重试，并发体验远不如智谱和直连 API）；第二是不支持退订退款；第三是夜间折扣要熬到 22:00 才生效；第四是双 Key 隔离机制很阴险，一旦配错成普通 sk- Key 就会直接去扣你的按量余额且不给退。
>
> DeepSeek 官方 API 直连（deepseek-flash 按量）
>
> 优势：2,500 并发上限随便开 20 个窗口狂飙；闲时（含午休 12-14点、晚 18点后 及周末全天）缓存读取只要 ¥0.02 / 百万，真·白菜价，余额永不过期。
>
> 真实账单：别信轻度用户吹的“几十块钱用半年”——把我这周智谱的负载原样套进 DS 官方价表，20.6 亿缓存确实只要 ¥44.2，但 1.11 亿未命中新输入要花掉 ¥122.0，加上输出 ¥18.4，单周实付 ¥184.65（折合重度跑满约 ¥790/月）。最适合留作多终端并发溢出时的弹性兜底池，而不是无脑全量裸跑。
>
> 海外顶配池（Google Ultra / Claude Max 等）
>
> 留给复杂架构设计和疑难杂症攻坚当主脑，拿来跑高频批量重构纯属浪费额度。
>
> ---
>
> https://linux.do#p-24946981-v2-11五、 给还在用智谱老版 V2 兄弟的续命操作
>
> 如果你手里的老版 V2 还没到期（注意智谱霸王条款：不想续费必须至少提前 3 天手动关自动续费，关了不影响用完当期），在到期前改两个动作，耐用度至少能翻一倍半：
>
> 严控单窗口上下文厚度在 200K 以内：在百炼和 DS 上可以一路干到底不清理，但在智谱 V2 上千万别养长会话。干完一个独立小任务哪怕才 150K 也立刻敲 /clear；如果大任务干到一半涨到了 200K+ 怕断思路，别用全文 /compact（会把刚写的代码细节也糊掉），直接在空输入框双击 Esc（/rewind），往上选当前子任务开头那条消息点 Summarize up to here——只切掉前面二十万字的陈年缓存，把最近正在改的鲜活上下文 100% 留住，立竿见影止血。
>
> 工作日 14:00–18:00 彻底停用智谱切别的池子：避开这 4 个小时的 3 倍惩罚，白捡回 20% 周配额。
>
> 以上全套实测数据留档备查，各位手头有老版 V2 账单的老哥也可以拉出来按 (闲时Token × 0.4 + 高峰Token × 1.2) 算一下，看看是不是全都精准卡死在整数池子上。

### [Google AI Ultra零元购的还有活着的吗](https://linux.do/t/topic/3199910)

`linuxdo:搞七捻三` · T2 · 2026-11-18 16:52 UTC · zh-CN · by Air Cyan

> [Current NVIDIA Driver Writes up to 30GB an Hour - Rollback to Fix - PC...](https://pcper.com/2026/11/current-nvidia-driver-writes-up-to-30gb-an-hour-rollback-to-fix/)

### [给 Sub2API 做了个降智巡检工具，以服务方式接入，不用改sub2api 支持自动剔除、冷却复测、通过恢复](https://linux.do/t/topic/3199739)

`linuxdo:开发调优` · T2 · 2026-11-18 15:59 UTC · zh-CN · by daqzia

> https://linux.do#p-24945165-h-1本帖使用社区开源推广，符合推广要求。我申明并遵循社区要求的以下内容：
>
> 我的帖子已经打上 [开源推广](https://linux.do/tag/2234-tag/2234) 标签： 是
>
> 我的开源项目完整开源，无未开源部分： 是
>
> 我的开源项目已链接认可 LINUX DO 社区： 是
>
> 我帖子内的项目介绍，AI生成、润色内容部分已截图发出： 是
>
> 以上选择我承诺是永久有效的，接受社区和佬友监督： 是
>
> 以下为项目介绍正文内容，AI生成、润色内容已使用截图方式发出
>
> ---
>
> 最近在折腾 Sub2API 的账号池，做了个模型质量巡检工具，分享给有同样需求的佬友。
>
> 一个分组里挂了好几个上游账号，接口都能正常返回，但有的账号碰到同一道题就是答不好。我想做的是让 Sub2API 自己定时出题、记录结果，发现异常就先把那个账号移出调度，等复测过了再放回来。
>
> https://linux.do#p-24945165-sub2api-2可以直接嵌进 Sub2API
>
> 巡检服务用 Docker Compose 单独部署，连上已有的 Sub2API，再加一个自定义菜单，就能在原来的面板里打开巡检页面。沿用 Sub2API 登录，无需改网关源码。 管理员可以配置巡检，普通用户也能选自己的 Key 测一轮。
>
> https://linux.do#p-24945165-h-3自动剔除后，怎么恢复？
>
> 举个例子，给一个分组设成每小时巡检一次，选一道逻辑题和一道 JSON 题。如果某个账号明确答错了标准答案题，开启自动剔除后，巡检就会暂时停用这个账号的调度。
>
> 冷却结束后，系统会单独复测原账号。这时候账号还在暂停调度，全部复测题通过才会恢复接单。 如果没通过，就继续冷却。遇到超时、限额之类的请求问题，巡检可以按优先级换同组账号，结果也会单独记录。
>
> 自动剔除默认关闭，可以先跑几轮看看结果，再决定要不要开。
>
> https://linux.do#p-24945165-h-4能测哪些题？
>
> 内置了糖果题、逻辑选择题、数值计算、JSON 指令遵循、指纹观察、鹈鹕骑自行车。每个分组可以多选题目，还能改题干、标准答案和每题请求次数。
>
> 有标准答案的题可以自动判。像「鹈鹕骑自行车」这类题，可以直接在结果页看 SVG 作品，也能翻历史，把不同时间的回答放在一起看。单轮答错适合当排查线索，判断模型表现有多稳定，可以多看几轮。
>
> 项目基于 NoonWake.AI 的 AI Drool Router 二次开发。欢迎佬友试用，尤其想听听大家平时都用什么题来测模型，或者希望巡检遇到什么情况时自动暂停账号。[项目地址](https://github.com/daQzi/code1024-drool-router)
>
> [![image](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/f/4/6/f466db09f1a14e0defb267c274b88be126e3f5be_2_690x341.jpeg)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/f/4/6/f466db09f1a14e0defb267c274b88be126e3f5be.jpeg)
>
> [![image](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/1/d/5/1d5e1e7d0a25d8c2b6c5accc8290682ce0d2d75f_2_690x341.jpeg)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/1/d/5/1d5e1e7d0a25d8c2b6c5accc8290682ce0d2d75f.jpeg)

### [【开源推广】Myco：在一个应用中连接使用在不同机器不同订阅的Agent，支持claude,codex,gemini等等](https://linux.do/t/topic/3199662)

`linuxdo:开发调优` · T2 · 2026-11-18 15:41 UTC · zh-CN · by glenn2033

> 开源推广 [（点击了解更多详细信息）](https://linux.do/t/topic/3199662/1)
> 项目地址：[Myco](https://github.com/chenhg5/myco)
>
> 包含Mac和Windows客户端，以及iOS移动端。
>
> https://linux.do#p-24944663-h-2背景
>
> 项目背景是我想薅A/羊毛，做一个能够让我远程调用claude.ai上的agent，薅claude羊毛的客户端，结果做着做着发现，我可以做一个管理不同订阅的客户端应用，把claude,codex,deepseek等等接一起，还支持手机端，而且这么久了，市面上很多客户端体验还很落后，于是想分享给大家试试。
>
> 当然如果你想无风险使用claude，也推荐你用myco。但你只想管理自己不同订阅的agent，放到一个地方，我相信这肯定是全网你能找到的体验最好的APP了（有点自吹自擂了，请轻喷，但真是矮子里面拔高个）。
>
> https://linux.do#p-24944663-h-3特性
>
> 支持有cli的agent接入，包括：claude code / codex / gemini / cursor 等等
>
> 支持没有cli的agent接入，包括：claude.ai 的 code agent / chatgpt work / grok bot / workbuddy / 千问办公 等等
>
> 支持agent们互相发现调用派活，比如 claude 给 deepseek 派活等
>
> 内置多种应用，办公套件，开发套件等等，甚至游戏，agent与你实时下棋，实时协作，agent可以自定义制作应用
>
> 支持自动化，自定义定时任务
>
> 支持语音实时聊天，在车上地铁上商场，吃饭，随时随地跟你的agent聊天
>
> 页面可以多开窗口
>
> 支持连接打开远程机器终端
>
> 支持类似 claude projects 的项目模式
>
> 支持手机端连接，随时派活
>
> https://linux.do#p-24944663-h-4截图
>

### [【小胡淘书纪】分享一些“有趣”的书名（第1期）](https://linux.do/t/topic/3199658)

`linuxdo:读书成诗` · T2 · 2026-11-18 15:39 UTC · zh-CN · by 小胡

> 每次写书评花的时间都比较久，加上最近只找书没怎么读书，
>
> 所以干脆水一期，如标题，本期分享一些我所见到的书籍：
>
> 他们各有特色，或是为了解决某一个具体问题，或是专门探讨某一项技能，或是书名很“标题党”但实际内容比较硬核，或是本身书名比较吸引我等等，其中大部分书籍我都没有完全阅读完，所以排名不分先后，佬们按需了解，感兴趣就可一读；
>
> https://linux.do#p-24944622-h-1同时欢迎各位佬在评论分享自己认为比较“有趣”的书籍
>
> 1、《植物的欲望》
>
> 原著《The Botany of Desire: A Plant’s-Eye View of the World》2001年英文版出版，【根据豆瓣书籍简介：本书讲述了苹果、郁金香、马铃薯等植物与人类之间的故事。】
>
> 被书籍名词所吸引，看英文名词也很有意思，植物的视角会是怎么样的呢；作者是加州大学伯克利分校的新闻学教授及科学和环境新闻学奈特项目的主任；
>
> 2、《一切皆契约· 真实世界中的博弈与决策》
>
> 被书名所吸引，契约让我联想社会契约论，博弈让我想起博弈论以及阅读过的《博弈论诡计》；
>
> 不过本书似乎是一本偏科普类经济学读本，把一些经济学概念糅杂进日常生活进行理解；
>
> 3、《章鱼的心灵》
>
> 被书名所吸引，自己曾经幻想过当一只小狗，本人是爱狗人士，而做一只章鱼或乌贼是怎样的？这个问题还是头一回见；
>
> 4、《侥幸求生· 阿尔·帕西诺自传》
>
> 被书名所吸引，本来是被前四个字吸引，没注意看副标题是自传，搜了发现是《教父》电影的演员的自传；
>
> 5、《半脑世界·一位脑科学家的中风体验》
>
> 被书名所吸引，原著是《My Stroke of Insight: A Brain Scientist’s Personal Journey》，英文原著于2006年1月出版；
>
> 这本书结合认知神经学，脑科学等书籍一起阅读会更好；
>
> 6、《脱稿讲话》
>
> 本书专门探讨脱稿讲话这个关键词；
>
> 作者是黄大钊，在北京有自己专门的沟通培训机构，这本书写了许多真实案例，可惜这本书是13年出版，放在现在看，可能会有一点过时；
>
> 在日常工作，尤其是到了大学，都避免不了上台作演讲，或是汇报，或是自我介绍；除此之外，在亲戚比较多的饭局上，同事比较多的饭局上等场景，也需要个人发表一些“客套话”；
>
> 上述这些场景，对于相对内向的佬友，会比较难，本书则是一定程度上可以帮助我们对付这些场景，为我们提供思路；
>
> 7、《江湖丛谈· 注音注释典藏本》
>
> 本书专门研究过去（清末民初）江湖上的行话，内幕
>
> 非常有特色的一本书，书里面举例的案例具有年代感，代入视角会感觉穿越回了民国时期；
>
> 在阅读江湖骗术的内容时，我会有一种熟悉的感觉，自己阅读过《影响力》《我们为什么会受骗》，这两本书都或多或少提及了如何防骗的内容。再联系到现实生活中，那些可恨的骗子，赚黑心钱的其实无处不在，阅读这些书籍也是为了保护自己，时刻谨惕这些坏人；
>
> 8、《农民进城防骗手册》
>
> 本书专门研究防骗，案例很多，相对系统
>
> 这本书于2006年8月出版，20年前的书，在具体案例上可能会有所过时，但是这本书胜在案例多，内容丰富，本书的作者虽然给这本书命名为农民防骗，实际上，人人都可以阅读！
>
> 防骗意识太重要了，坑你钱的坏人会让你感觉他不是刻意坑你钱，甚至等你转出钱的那一刻起，你还会抱有希望，直到发现被拉黑；这类书的存在意义是非常大的！
>
> 以上是第一期，事实上我近年来认识了非常多“有趣”的书籍，但是很多书都没来得及看，这个系列也算是主动进行总结，到时候空出时间，可能会第一时间去看看；
>
> 最后欢迎各位佬分享自己喜欢的“有趣”书籍！爱你们！
